Many defense and intelligence contractors require a security clearance, which the employer sponsors after hiring. You cannot apply for one on your own, so roles that ask for an active clearance often go to people who held one in the military or government.
Time it takes

Entry-level roles are open to new graduates. Becoming an independent contracts manager usually takes several years of handling bids, negotiations and contract changes. Former federal contract specialists often move to company roles after a few years in government.
qa: What certification is best for government contracts?

No certification is required, but the National Contract Management Association’s Certified Federal Contracts Manager (CFCM) is widely recognized for federal work, and its Certified Professional Contracts Manager (CPCM) covers broader contract management. Federal employees earn the Federal Acquisition Certification in Contracting (FAC-C) through their agencies, and contractors value that experience.
Can you become a government contracts specialist without experience?

Yes, at the entry level. Contractors hire new graduates as contracts or subcontracts administrators, and federal agencies hire contract specialist trainees, often through intern or development programs. A degree with business coursework, knowledge of the Federal Acquisition Regulation and strong attention to detail help. A security clearance opens more defense roles.

steps: Education

Most people earn a bachelor’s degree in computer science, computer engineering or electrical engineering. Key courses include computer architecture, operating systems, compilers, parallel programming and linear algebra. Many employers in AI hardware and research favor a master’s or PhD, especially for roles tied to compilers or chip design.
Core programming skills

Build strong C and C++ skills, plus Python for AI work. Learn GPU programming with CUDA or similar models, and study memory hierarchies, threading and vector instructions. Practice with profilers to find bottlenecks and measure speedups instead of guessing.
No license required

There is no state license, required exam or standard certification for this work. Employers judge candidates by degrees, past projects and technical interviews that test low-level coding, architecture knowledge and the ability to explain why code is slow.
Projects and portfolio

Write and tune your own GPU kernels, such as matrix multiply or attention, and publish benchmarks. Contributing performance fixes to open-source machine learning frameworks, compilers or scientific computing libraries is one of the most convincing ways to show real skill.
First job

Common entry points are internships and junior roles in high-performance computing, compiler teams, graphics or game engines, or machine learning infrastructure. Many people start as general software engineers and move into performance work after taking on optimization tasks.
Time it takes

Expect four years for a bachelor’s degree, then usually two to five years of related experience before holding a dedicated performance engineering title. A graduate degree with research in parallel computing or compilers can shorten the path into specialist roles.
qa: Do you need a degree to become a GPU performance engineer?

Most employers expect a bachelor’s degree in computer science, computer engineering or electrical engineering, and many prefer a master’s or PhD. Without a degree, a strong record of open-source performance work, published benchmarks and deep C++ and GPU programming skill can still open doors, but it is a harder path.
Is there a certification for GPU programming?

No certification is required or widely expected for GPU performance roles in the US. Some vendor training courses exist, but hiring decisions rest mainly on technical interviews, education and proof of work, such as optimized kernels, profiling results and contributions to compilers or machine learning frameworks.

steps: Education

Most employers look for a bachelor’s degree in graphic design, visual communication or a related art field. A two-year associate degree or a certificate program can also get you started. Coursework covers typography, color, layout, branding and design history.
Design software

Learn the standard tools: Adobe Illustrator, Photoshop and InDesign for print and brand work, and Figma for web pages and slides. Adobe offers optional Adobe Certified Professional exams, but most employers judge your skill from your work, not a certificate.
No license required

There is no license, registration or required exam to work as a graphic or brand designer in any US state. Anyone can call themselves a designer, so your portfolio does the job a license does in other fields.
Portfolio

Build an online portfolio of your best projects, such as logos, ad campaigns, brand guidelines and web layouts. Show your process from rough sketches to final files. Class work, personal projects and small freelance jobs for local businesses all count.
First job

Most people start as a design intern, junior graphic designer or production artist. The work is preparing files, resizing ads and following an existing brand’s rules. Brand designer roles that create whole visual identities usually come after a few years of this work.
Time it takes

Expect about four years for a bachelor’s degree or two for an associate degree, plus time to build a portfolio. Moving from a junior role to brand designer usually takes several more years of paid work.
qa: Do you need a degree to be a graphic designer?

Most job postings ask for a bachelor’s degree in graphic design or a related field, but it is not legally required. Some designers get hired with an associate degree, a certificate or self-taught skills. In every case, a strong portfolio that shows real projects and clear thinking is what usually wins the job.
How long does it take to become a graphic designer?

Most people take two to four years, depending on whether they earn an associate or bachelor’s degree, then start in a junior or production role. Self-taught designers can move faster if they build a solid portfolio. Leading brand projects on your own usually takes several more years of hands-on experience.

steps: Education

Most graphics engineers earn a bachelor’s degree in computer science, computer engineering, math or physics. Key courses are linear algebra, calculus, data structures and a computer graphics class. Research, GPU architecture and advanced rendering roles often go to people with a master’s degree or PhD.
Core technical skills

Learn C++ well, since most rendering code uses it. Then learn a graphics API such as Vulkan, DirectX 12, Metal or OpenGL, and a shader language like HLSL or GLSL. Study how GPUs work, including memory, parallelism and performance profiling.
Build a portfolio

Employers want proof you can make pixels appear. Write a software ray tracer, a rasterizer or a small real-time renderer with lighting, shadows and post effects. Share the code publicly and record short videos showing results and frame times.
No license required

There is no license, registration or required certification for this work in the US. Hiring depends on your code, portfolio and technical interviews, which often include 3D math, rendering pipeline questions and C++ problems.
First job

Common entry points are junior graphics, engine or tools programmer roles at game studios, or entry-level software jobs at companies making GPUs, simulation, visual effects or VR products. Some start as general or gameplay programmers and move into rendering later.
Time it takes

Expect about four years for a degree plus one to two years of focused graphics projects before a first rendering job. Senior roles leading renderer design usually come after several more years of shipped work.
qa: Do you need a degree to become a graphics engineer?

Most employers expect a bachelor’s degree in computer science, math or a related field, because the work relies on linear algebra and low-level programming. A strong portfolio of renderers and shader work can sometimes replace a degree, especially at game studios. Research and GPU hardware roles more often ask for a master’s degree or PhD.
How long does it take to become a graphics engineer?

It usually takes four to six years. That covers a four-year degree plus time building graphics projects such as a ray tracer or real-time renderer. Many people also spend a year or two in a general programming or gameplay role before moving onto a dedicated rendering team.

steps: Education

No degree, license or diploma is required. Many associates are high school students or recent graduates. Basic reading, simple math, counting change and a friendly manner with customers matter more than formal schooling.
Age and work permit
Federal law lets 14 and 15 year olds work in retail with limits on hours, but many stores hire from 16. Some states require minors to get a work permit or age certificate before starting.
Food and alcohol rules

Some states and counties require a food handler card for deli, bakery or meat counter work. The minimum age to sell or ring up alcohol varies by state, and some states require responsible alcohol seller training.
On-the-job training

Stores train new hires themselves, usually over a few days to two weeks. You learn the register, stocking and rotating products, safe lifting and box cutter use. Federal rules bar workers under 18 from driving forklifts.
First job
Most people start as a bagger, courtesy clerk, cashier or night stocker. Reliable workers often move to a counter such as deli, produce or bakery, then to shift lead or department lead.
Time it takes
You can usually be hired within one to three weeks of applying and work alone after your first week or two. Moving up to a lead role often takes a year or two of steady work.
qa: Do you need experience to work at a grocery store?

No. Grocery store associate is one of the most common first jobs in the US. Stores train new hires on the register, stocking and safety. Showing up on time, being polite to customers and being able to stand and lift for a full shift matter more than past work.
How old do you have to be to work at a grocery store?

Federal law allows 14 and 15 year olds to work in grocery stores with limits on hours and tasks, but many stores hire from 16. Selling alcohol has a separate minimum age that varies by state, and some states require minors to get a work permit first.

steps: Education

Most people hold a bachelor’s degree in computer science, engineering, business, economics or design. No license, registration or required exam exists for this work. Some add an MBA, often mid-career, but many group and principal product managers do not have one.
First job

Common ways in are associate product manager programs for new graduates, or a move into a product manager title from software engineering, UX design, data analysis, consulting or customer-facing roles, often inside the same company.
Years as product manager

Spend several years owning a product or feature area from start to finish: customer research, roadmaps, work with engineering and design, launches and metrics. Promotion to senior product manager usually follows a record of shipped products with measurable results.
Choose lead or specialist

The path splits here. Group product managers hire, coach and manage a team of product managers. Principal product managers usually stay individual contributors but own the most complex or cross-team product area. Both need strong strategy skills and influence with executives.
Time it takes

Most people reach this level after roughly eight or more years of work, with much of it in product management. Optional certificates in product or agile practice exist, but employers weigh a proven track record far more heavily.
qa: Do you need a certification to be a group product manager?

No. There is no license, required exam or standard certification for group or principal product managers in the US. Employers look for years of product management experience, products you have shipped, measurable results and, for group roles, experience managing or mentoring other product managers. Optional product or agile certificates can help early on but rarely decide a hire at this level.
How long does it take to become a principal product manager?

It usually takes about eight or more years of work experience, much of it as a product manager and then senior product manager. People typically start as associate product managers or move over from engineering, design or analytics. Moving up depends on owning larger, more complex product areas and showing results across teams, not on any formal exam or degree.

steps: Education

Most growth engineers hold a bachelor’s degree in computer science, software engineering or a related field. Some are self-taught or come through short coding programs. Employers care most that you can ship production code for web or mobile apps.
Experimentation and data skills

Learn A/B testing, basic statistics such as sample size and significance, and SQL. Get comfortable with product analytics and event tracking. Growth work means proving whether a change to sign-up, onboarding or referral flows actually moved a metric.
No license required

There is no license, registration or required exam for growth engineering in any state. Certifications are optional and rarely decide hiring. A record of shipped features and measured results counts for much more.
Portfolio of shipped work

Build and launch your own projects, then run real experiments on them, such as testing two sign-up pages or adding a referral link. Write up what you tried, what you measured and what happened. Interviewers often ask for exactly these stories.
First job

Most people start as a general software engineer, often full-stack or front-end, at a consumer app or software-as-a-service company. Many move onto a growth team after working on onboarding, pricing pages, emails or notifications.
Time it takes

After a degree or self-study, people often spend two to four years as software engineers before taking a dedicated growth engineer title. Moving faster is possible at small startups, where engineers frequently own growth work from the start.
qa: Do you need a degree to be a growth engineer?

No degree is legally required, and there is no license. Many growth engineers do have a computer science or related degree, and some employers prefer one. Others hire self-taught developers who can show shipped code, solid SQL and a track record of experiments that improved sign-ups, activation or retention.
What is the difference between a growth engineer and a software engineer?

A growth engineer is a software engineer whose work is judged by user metrics. Instead of building core product features, they build and test sign-up flows, onboarding, referral programs and paywalls. The job adds A/B testing, analytics and close work with product and marketing teams to the usual coding skills.

steps: Education

Most growth managers hold a bachelor’s degree in marketing, business, economics, statistics, computer science or a related field. No single degree is required. Coursework in statistics, data analysis and consumer behavior helps most, since the job centers on running experiments and reading the results.
Core skills

Learn to design A/B tests, write basic SQL, read product analytics dashboards and build simple funnel models. Familiarity with paid acquisition, email, SEO, onboarding flows and pricing tests is expected. Many people build these skills through online courses and side projects as well as on the job.
No license required

There is no license, registration or required exam for growth work in the US. Vendor certificates, such as those for analytics or ad platforms, are optional. Employers care more about a record of experiments you ran and the measurable results they produced.
First job

People usually start as a growth marketing associate, marketing analyst, product analyst, performance marketing specialist or lifecycle marketing coordinator. Some move over from data analysis, product management or engineering roles at startups, where small teams let them run tests on acquisition, activation and retention early.
Build a track record

Keep a written log of tests: the hypothesis, the setup, the metric and the outcome, including failures. This becomes your portfolio. Hiring managers often ask candidates to walk through a past experiment or to propose tests for their product during interviews.
Time it takes

Moving into a growth manager title usually takes about three to five years of hands-on work after college. Strong results at a fast-growing company can shorten that path, while larger companies may expect more years and experience managing a budget or a small team.
qa: Do you need a degree to be a growth manager?

Most employers prefer a bachelor’s degree in marketing, business, economics, statistics, computer science or a similar field, but none is legally required. Some growth managers come from unrelated majors or no degree at all. What matters most is proof that you can run experiments, analyze data and grow users or revenue in measurable ways.
How long does it take to become a growth manager?

It usually takes about three to five years of experience in roles like marketing analyst, product analyst or growth marketing associate. During that time you build skills in A/B testing, SQL and analytics, and collect a record of experiments with clear results. Startups sometimes promote people faster when their tests drive visible growth.

steps: Education

No degree is required by law, but most employers ask for a bachelor’s degree. Common fields are marketing, business, economics, statistics or communications. People from other fields get in too if they can show they understand data, ad platforms and testing.
No license needed

Growth marketing has no state license, registration or required exam in the US. Hiring managers judge you on results you can show, such as campaigns you ran, tests you designed and the numbers they moved.
Core skills and tools

Learn to run paid search and social ads, build email campaigns and set up A/B tests. Get comfortable with web analytics, spreadsheets and basic SQL. Optional free certifications, such as Google Ads and Google Analytics certifications, can show employers you know the tools.
Build proof of results

Run small campaigns for a side project, a local business or a nonprofit. Track spend, sign-ups and cost per customer. A short write-up of each experiment, what you changed and what happened, works as your portfolio in interviews.
First job

Most people start in a narrower role, such as marketing coordinator, paid media specialist, email marketing specialist, SEO specialist or marketing analyst. These jobs teach one channel deeply and how to report on its return.
Time it takes

Expect about four years for a degree, then usually two to four years in an entry-level channel or analyst role before moving into a growth marketer title. Startups sometimes hire into growth roles sooner if you can show strong results.
qa: Do you need a degree to become a growth marketer?

Not always. Most job postings prefer a bachelor’s degree in marketing, business, economics or a related field, but there is no legal requirement. Many growth marketers come from other backgrounds and get hired by showing real campaign results, test write-ups and skill with ad platforms, analytics tools and spreadsheets.
How long does it take to become a growth marketer?

Most people take about two to four years after college. They usually start in an entry-level role like marketing coordinator, paid media specialist or marketing analyst, learn one channel well, then take on testing and budget decisions across several channels. Strong results at a startup can shorten that path.

steps: Education

Most growth product managers hold a bachelor’s degree in business, computer science, economics, statistics, psychology or a related field. No single degree is required. Some later earn an MBA, but employers rarely require one for this role.
Analytics and experiment skills

Learn SQL, spreadsheet modeling and the statistics behind A/B testing, such as sample size and significance. Get comfortable with funnels, cohorts, retention curves and product analytics tools. Hiring managers often test these skills directly in interviews.
No license required

There is no license, registration or required exam for this work in the US. Private providers offer product management and growth certificates, but employers treat them as optional. A record of shipped experiments with measured results counts far more.
First job

Most people move in from a related role: associate product manager, growth or lifecycle marketer, data or product analyst, or software engineer on a growth team. Running and measuring experiments in that job builds the track record you need.
Time it takes

It commonly takes two to five years of work after college to land the title. Many people first spend time as a general product manager or in a growth-focused analyst or marketing role before moving into growth product management.
qa: Do you need a degree to become a growth product manager?

Most growth product managers have a bachelor’s degree, often in business, computer science, economics or statistics, and many job postings ask for one. No specific major is required, and there is no license. Strong SQL, experimentation skills and proof that your past changes moved signups, activation or retention can matter as much as the degree itself.
How long does it take to become a growth product manager?

It usually takes two to five years after college. Most people start in a related job such as product analyst, growth marketer, software engineer or associate product manager. After building a record of experiments that improved user numbers or revenue, they move into a growth product manager role, either at the same company or a new one.

steps: Bachelor’s degree

Most hardware engineers earn a bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering or computer engineering. Employers often prefer programs accredited by ABET. Core courses cover circuits, digital logic, signals, electronics, computer architecture and programming. A strong base in math and physics matters from the start.
Internships and projects

Internships and co-op terms during school are the most common way into the field. Hands-on projects also help: building and debugging circuit boards, writing Verilog or VHDL for FPGAs, and running circuit simulations. A portfolio of working designs shows employers you can take a design from idea to tested hardware.
Master’s degree for chip design

Many chip design roles, such as ASIC design, verification and analog circuit design, expect a master’s degree in electrical or computer engineering. It usually takes one to two more years. Board-level and test roles more often hire with a bachelor’s degree alone.
Optional PE license

No license is needed for most hardware engineering jobs in private industry. Some engineers still pass the NCEES FE exam after graduating and later earn a state Professional Engineer (PE) license. Requirements vary by state and usually include several years of supervised work. It matters mostly for public projects or consulting.
Time it takes

Plan on about four years for a bachelor’s degree, plus one to two years if you pursue a master’s degree. Moving from an entry-level role to leading designs on your own usually takes several more years of work experience.
First job

Common first jobs include junior or associate hardware engineer, test engineer, validation engineer and design verification engineer. These roles involve testing boards and chips, writing test plans, debugging in the lab and supporting senior engineers on layouts and schematics.
qa: Do you need a license to be a hardware engineer?

Most hardware engineers do not need a license. Companies that design chips, boards and devices hire based on your degree and skills. A state Professional Engineer (PE) license is optional. It requires passing the NCEES FE and PE exams plus supervised experience, and it matters mainly for public work or consulting. Requirements vary by state.
How long does it take to become a hardware engineer?

It usually takes about four years to earn a bachelor’s degree in electrical or computer engineering and land an entry-level job. Many chip design roles prefer a master’s degree, which adds one to two years. Internships during school can shorten the job search after graduation.

steps: Education

Most hardware program managers hold a bachelor’s degree in electrical, mechanical, industrial or manufacturing engineering. Some come from physics or materials science. A master’s degree or MBA helps for some roles but is not required. Courses in manufacturing processes, statistics and supply chain are especially useful.
First job

The usual way in is a hands-on engineering role: hardware, mechanical, electrical, manufacturing, test or product design engineer. There you learn build phases such as EVT, DVT and PVT, design for manufacturing, failure analysis, and how to work with suppliers and contract manufacturers.
Step into program work

Many engineers move over through roles like NPI engineer, supplier quality engineer or a program manager on a smaller product. You take ownership of schedules, bills of materials, build plans and cross-team decisions. Expect frequent factory visits, often overseas, during prototype and production builds.
No license required

There is no state license or required exam for this work. Some people earn the PMP from PMI, which requires documented project experience and an exam. Lean Six Sigma training or the ASCM CPIM can also help. Employers usually care most about products you have helped ship.
Time it takes

Expect four years of college plus several years of engineering or manufacturing work before a first hardware program manager title. Many people make the move after three to eight years, depending on how many products they have taken from prototype to mass production.
qa: Do you need a PMP to be a hardware program manager?

No. The PMP from PMI is optional and few hardware employers require it. Some list it as a plus. Hiring managers usually look for an engineering background and proof that you have taken a physical product through prototype builds into mass production with factories and suppliers.
How long does it take to become a hardware program manager?

It usually takes a four-year engineering degree followed by several years of work as a hardware, mechanical, electrical or manufacturing engineer. Many people move into the role after three to eight years, once they have helped ship products and have led schedules, builds or supplier work on real projects.

steps: Education

Technicians usually start with a high school diploma, and many add a certificate or associate degree in electronics or electrical technology. Engineers usually need a bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, mechanical engineering or electrical engineering technology, with coursework in circuits, power distribution and CAD.
Hands-on wiring skills

Everyone in this work learns to read schematics and wiring diagrams, cut and strip wire, crimp terminals, solder, and insert pins into connectors. You also learn to use continuity testers, pull testers and harness test boards to check that every circuit is correct.
Industry certification

No state license is required. Many employers expect or provide training to the IPC/WHMA-A-620 standard, often as a Certified IPC Specialist (CIS). J-STD-001 certification for soldering is common too. Aerospace and defense work also follows military specifications.
Design tools and standards

Engineers learn electrical CAD and 3D harness routing tools, wire gauge and fuse sizing, connector selection, and drawings for the shop floor. Automotive work follows SAE standards, while aerospace and defense work follows military and customer specifications.
First job

Many technicians start as harness assemblers or production technicians and move up to testing, rework or prototype building. New engineers often start as junior harness design engineers or in manufacturing or test engineering at a vehicle, equipment or aerospace supplier.
Time it takes

An assembler can be trained in a few weeks, and becoming a skilled technician usually takes one to two years. Engineers spend about four years on a degree, then usually two to four years on the job before leading harness designs.
qa: Do you need a license to be a wire harness engineer?

No. There is no state license for wire harness work. Employers often expect training to the IPC/WHMA-A-620 standard, and many offer it on the job. Engineers usually hold a bachelor’s degree in electrical or mechanical engineering. A Professional Engineer license is rarely required for this kind of design work in industry.
How long does it take to become a wire harness technician?

Entry-level harness assemblers can be trained in a few weeks on the job. Becoming a skilled technician who builds prototypes, reads complex drawings and troubleshoots failures usually takes one to two years. A certificate or associate degree in electronics, plus IPC/WHMA-A-620 training, can help you move up faster.

steps: Education

Most marketing leaders hold a bachelor’s degree in marketing, business, communications or a related field. There is no required major. Some later earn an MBA, which many employers like for CMO roles but rarely demand outright.
First job

People usually start as a marketing coordinator, marketing specialist or associate in areas like digital marketing, brand, content or product marketing. Early roles teach campaign execution, analytics and working with sales teams.
Build management experience

The next steps are marketing manager, then senior manager or director. At these levels you own a budget, hire and lead a team, and answer for measurable results such as pipeline, revenue or customer growth.
Certifications

No license, registration or exam is required to lead marketing in the US. Some people take optional courses or certificates in digital marketing, analytics or marketing platforms, but employers weigh a record of results far more heavily.
Time it takes

Reaching head of marketing usually takes ten to fifteen years of marketing work, often with several years as a director. At small companies and startups, people may step into the top marketing role sooner.
qa: Do you need an MBA to become a CMO?

No. An MBA is not required to become a chief marketing officer. Many CMOs have one, and some larger companies prefer it. Most employers care more about years of leadership, budget ownership and a proven record of growing revenue or customers than about a specific degree.
How long does it take to become a head of marketing?

It usually takes ten to fifteen years. Most people start in an entry-level marketing role, move up to manager and then director, and take on team and budget responsibility along the way. The path can be faster at startups and small companies, where the top marketing job may open with less experience.

steps: Education

There is no required degree, license or exam for this work. Most heads of product hold a bachelor’s degree in computer science, engineering, business, economics or design. Some add an MBA, which can help in business-focused companies but is rarely required.
First job

Most people start as an associate product manager or product manager. Many others move over from a related role such as software engineer, UX designer, data analyst, product marketer or customer success manager, then shift into product work inside the same company.
Product manager experience

Spend several years owning a product or feature area. You work with engineers and designers, talk to customers, read usage data, set priorities and ship releases. Employers look for a clear record of products you launched and the results they produced.
Managing product managers

The usual next steps are senior product manager, group product manager and director of product. In these roles you hire and coach other product managers, set a roadmap across several teams and present plans to executives. Experience leading people is expected before a head of product role.
Time it takes

Reaching head of product usually takes eight years or more of work, with several of those years spent managing product managers. People sometimes get there faster at small startups, where the first product hire may carry the title early.
qa: Do you need a certification to become a head of product?

No. There is no license, exam or certification required to work as a head of product in the US. Private product management courses and certificates exist, but employers rarely ask for them. Hiring managers care more about years of product experience, products you shipped, measurable results and a record of leading other product managers.
How long does it take to become a head of product?

It usually takes eight years or more. Most people spend several years as a product manager, then move up to senior product manager, group product manager or director before leading the whole product team. At a small startup the path can be shorter, while large companies often expect more years and broader management experience.

steps: Two paths

Dietitians and health coaches work in the same area but enter very differently. Registered dietitian nutritionists follow a regulated path with degrees, supervised practice and a national exam. Health coaching has no license, and most coaches enter through a training program and an optional national certification.
Dietitian education

Since 2024, candidates for the registered dietitian nutritionist (RDN) credential need a graduate degree. They also complete coursework from a program accredited by ACEND, the Accreditation Council for Education in Nutrition and Dietetics. A bachelor’s degree in nutrition, dietetics or food science is the usual start.
Supervised practice

Future dietitians complete at least 1,000 hours of supervised practice in hospitals, community programs and food service. Some graduate programs build this in, while others are followed by a separate dietetic internship. Candidates then pass the national registration exam from the Commission on Dietetic Registration.
State license

Most states license or certify dietitians, and many restrict individualized nutrition counseling to licensed professionals. Requirements vary by state, so health coaches should check what advice their state allows. Dietitians renew the RDN credential with continuing education.
Coach certification

Health coaches often take a training program of several months, then may earn the National Board Certified Health & Wellness Coach (NBC-HWC) credential, which requires an approved program, logged coaching sessions and an exam. Other certifications come from fitness and wellness groups. Many coaches also have a nursing, fitness or nutrition background.
First job and timeline

New dietitians often start as clinical dietitians in hospitals or long-term care, about six years after high school. Health coaches can start within a year, often at health plans, employer wellness programs, clinics or digital health companies, or by building their own client base.
qa: How long does it take to become a registered dietitian?

Usually about six years after high school. You need a bachelor’s degree, a graduate degree, which has been required since 2024, and at least 1,000 hours of supervised practice through an ACEND-accredited program. Then you pass the national exam from the Commission on Dietetic Registration and, in most states, apply for a state license.
Do you need a license to be a health coach?

No state licenses health coaches. Many earn a certification such as the NBC-HWC from the National Board for Health & Wellness Coaching. Coaches must stay within their scope, because many states limit individualized nutrition advice and medical nutrition therapy to licensed dietitians or other licensed professionals. Rules vary by state.

steps: Pick a clinical or support path

Health-tech and biotech companies hire licensed clinicians who treat patients, often by telehealth, and support staff such as medical assistants, care coordinators and clinical research coordinators. Your path depends on which side you choose. Treating patients requires a clinical license. Support roles usually do not.
Education

Registered nurses complete an associate or bachelor’s degree in nursing. Nurse practitioners add a master’s or doctoral nursing degree. Physicians finish medical school and a residency. Medical assistants often take a certificate program lasting under a year to two years. Coordinator roles usually ask for a bachelor’s degree in a health or science field.
Exams and state license

Nurses pass the NCLEX-RN and get licensed by a state board of nursing. Physicians pass the USMLE or COMLEX series and hold a state medical license. Nurse practitioner rules vary by state, and many states require national board certification. Medical assistant certification, such as the CMA, is optional but often preferred.
Clinical experience

Most companies want clinicians with prior hands-on experience in a hospital or clinic before they work remotely or with less supervision. Many nurses and providers spend a few years in bedside or outpatient care first. Support staff often gain experience in a medical office, research site or patient services role.
Licenses in more states

Telehealth clinicians generally must be licensed in the state where the patient is located. Nurses in states that join the Nurse Licensure Compact can hold one multistate license. Physicians may use the Interstate Medical Licensure Compact to apply in member states. Employers often help pay for or manage extra licenses.
First job

Common ways in are a staff nurse or clinic provider job, then a move to a telehealth or virtual care company. Non-clinical people often start as a medical assistant, patient care coordinator or clinical research assistant, then grow into coordinator, operations or clinical support roles.
qa: Do you need a license to work in healthcare at a health-tech company?

It depends on the role. Anyone who diagnoses, treats or gives clinical advice, such as a nurse, nurse practitioner or physician, needs an active state license, usually in each state where their patients are. Support roles like care coordinator or patient services usually need no license, though some employers prefer a certification.
How long does it take to become a telehealth nurse?

Becoming a registered nurse usually takes two to four years of nursing school, followed by passing the NCLEX-RN and getting a state license. Most telehealth employers then want some hands-on hospital or clinic experience first, so many nurses spend a few more years in direct patient care before moving into virtual work.

steps: Education

Most start with a bachelor’s degree in health administration, business, public health or nursing. Senior roles in hospitals and health systems often ask for a master’s degree, such as a Master of Health Administration (MHA), an MBA or an MPH. MHA programs are accredited by CAHME.
First job

Common entry roles are practice coordinator, patient access supervisor, department coordinator, billing supervisor or assistant to an executive. Nurses often move into administration through charge nurse and unit manager roles. Many MHA graduates enter through paid administrative fellowships of one to two years.
Nursing home license

Some settings require a license. Every state licenses nursing home administrators, usually requiring a degree, an administrator-in-training period and the national exam from NAB, the National Association of Long Term Care Administrator Boards. Many states also license assisted living administrators. Requirements vary by state.
Certification

Hospital and practice administration have no license, but certifications help. The American College of Healthcare Executives awards Fellow (FACHE) status after years of experience and an exam. The Medical Group Management Association offers the Certified Medical Practice Executive (CMPE) for practice managers.
Compliance knowledge

Administrators must know HIPAA privacy and security rules, billing and coding basics, labor and staffing laws, and the standards of accreditors such as The Joint Commission. This knowledge usually comes on the job, through workshops or through a graduate program.
Time it takes

A practice manager role often follows three to five years of experience after a bachelor’s degree. Department director and executive roles usually take five to ten years or more, often with a master’s degree. A nursing home license adds a training period whose length varies by state.
qa: Do you need a license to be a healthcare administrator?

Only in some settings. Every state requires nursing home administrators to be licensed, usually after an administrator-in-training period and the NAB national exam, and many states license assisted living administrators. Hospital, clinic and medical practice administrators need no license, though certifications such as FACHE or CMPE can help.
How long does it take to become a healthcare administrator?

Entry-level coordinator jobs are open right after a bachelor’s degree. Most people reach practice manager after three to five years of experience. Hospital department directors and executives usually have a master’s degree, such as an MHA, and five to ten or more years of experience, sometimes after a one- to two-year administrative fellowship.

steps: Education

Most employers ask for a high school diploma or GED. Many entry-level hires also have an IT certificate or an associate degree in information technology or computer support from a community college. A bachelor’s degree helps but is rarely required for this role.
Hands-on practice

Learn the basics people call about: resetting passwords, setting up laptops, fixing printers, installing software and troubleshooting Wi-Fi. Many people build a home lab, help family or volunteer to practice. Customer service experience counts too, since most of the job is talking people through problems.
Certification

No license is required. Many employers prefer or ask for CompTIA A+, the most common entry certification for support work. It takes two exams. Some people add CompTIA Network+ or ITIL 4 Foundation later to show they understand networks and how IT service desks run.
Time it takes

Someone starting from scratch usually takes three months to a year of study and practice to get hired. An associate degree takes about two years. People who already have retail, call center or customer service experience often move in faster.
First job

The usual first job is Tier 1 help desk or service desk analyst, often on contract or through a staffing agency. IT internships and campus tech support jobs are other ways in. From there, people move to desktop support, Tier 2, systems administration or networking.
qa: Do you need a certification to work at a help desk?

No license or certification is legally required. Still, many employers list CompTIA A+ as preferred or required for entry-level help desk jobs, and it can help you stand out if you have no IT work history. Some employers will hire without it if you show solid troubleshooting skills and good customer service experience.
How long does it take to become a help desk technician?

Usually a few months to two years. Self-study plus a certification like CompTIA A+ can get someone ready in three months to a year. An associate degree in IT takes about two years. Prior customer service work often shortens the path, since employers value people who stay calm and explain things clearly.

steps: Education

No degree is required for most hospitality jobs. A high school diploma or GED helps, and some high schools offer culinary or hospitality classes. People who want to move into chef or management roles often take a certificate or associate degree in culinary arts or hospitality management, but many learn entirely on the job.
Food handler card

Many states and counties require workers who handle food to get a food handler card within a set time after hiring. It usually means a short online course and test. Requirements vary by state, and some employers ask for one even where it is not required by law.
Alcohol server training

If you will serve or sell alcohol, some states require responsible beverage service training, and many employers expect it everywhere. Common programs include ServSafe Alcohol and TIPS. Minimum age rules for serving alcohol also differ by state, so check local law before applying for bar or server roles.
First job

Most people start as a dishwasher, prep cook, line cook, server assistant, host or housekeeping attendant. These roles teach kitchen safety, speed, guest service and teamwork. Company kitchens, hotels, restaurants and travel teams all hire beginners and train them on site.
Manager certification

To run a shift or a kitchen, you will often need a Certified Food Protection Manager credential, such as ServSafe Manager. Most states follow the FDA Food Code, which expects a certified person in charge at many food businesses. Experienced cooks can also pursue American Culinary Federation certifications.
Time it takes

You can start an entry level job within days or weeks once you have any required food handler card. Moving up to lead cook, shift supervisor or sous chef usually takes two to five years of steady work, depending on the employer and your skills.
qa: Do you need a license to work in hospitality?

Most hospitality jobs need no state license. Many states or counties do require a food handler card for anyone who prepares or serves food, and some require alcohol server training. Supervisors and kitchen managers often need a food protection manager certification. Requirements vary by state and city, so check local health department rules.
Do you need culinary school to become a cook?

No. Many cooks start as dishwashers or prep cooks and learn on the job, moving up as they gain speed and skill. Culinary school or an associate degree can teach techniques and help with advancement, but employers usually care most about hands-on kitchen experience, reliability and food safety knowledge.

steps: Requirements

Most guest service jobs ask for a high school diploma or GED and good communication skills. No license is required. Speaking a second language, especially Spanish, is a plus in many markets. Weekend, holiday and night shifts are common.
First job

Typical first jobs are front desk agent, guest service agent, reservations agent, bell attendant, room attendant or night auditor. Many employers hire people without hotel experience if they have customer service work in retail or restaurants.
On-the-job training

Training usually lasts a few days to a few weeks. You learn the property management system used for reservations and check-in, payment handling, loyalty programs, safety procedures and how to resolve complaints. Some employers also teach upselling and group bookings.
Certification

Certification is optional. The American Hotel & Lodging Educational Institute offers credentials such as Certified Guest Service Professional. Concierges with years of experience may seek membership in Les Clefs d’Or USA, a professional association of hotel concierges.
Moving up

With experience, many move to front desk supervisor, front office manager or guest services manager. A degree in hospitality management or a hotel company’s management training program can speed up the path toward assistant general manager and general manager roles.
Time it takes

You can start in a few weeks. Reaching supervisor usually takes one to three years, and front office manager several years. General manager roles typically follow many years in hotel operations across several departments.
qa: Can you work at a hotel front desk without experience?

Yes. Many hotels hire front desk and guest service agents with no hotel experience and train them on the job in reservations software, check-in and payment handling. Experience in retail, restaurants or other customer service work helps. Employers look for a friendly manner, clear communication and willingness to work evenings, weekends and holidays.
How long does it take to become a hotel manager?

Usually several years. Many managers start as front desk agents and move up to supervisor in one to three years, then front office manager. Hospitality management graduates and management trainees can move faster. Becoming general manager of a full hotel usually takes many years of experience across departments.

steps: Education

Most employers ask for a bachelor’s degree in human resources, business administration, psychology, or a related field. A master’s in HR or an MBA can help for senior or large-company roles, but it is rarely required to get started.
First HR job

Most people start as an HR assistant, HR coordinator, or recruiting coordinator. These roles teach onboarding, employee records, benefits questions, and HR systems, and they show how policies work day to day.
Generalist experience

The usual next step is HR generalist. Here you handle employee relations cases, investigations, performance reviews, leaves, and pay questions. You also learn federal employment law such as FLSA, FMLA, and Title VII, plus the rules in your state.
Professional certification

No license is required. Many employers prefer a certification, such as SHRM-CP or SHRM-SCP from SHRM, or PHR or SPHR from HRCI. Each requires passing an exam, and eligibility rules differ by credential.
Time it takes

Moving into an HR business partner role usually takes about five to eight years of HR experience. Employers want proof that you can advise managers on org changes, performance problems, and difficult cases without close supervision.
qa: Do you need a certification to be an HR business partner?

No license or certification is legally required. Many job postings still prefer one, most often SHRM-CP or SHRM-SCP from SHRM, or PHR or SPHR from HRCI. A credential shows employment law and HR knowledge, but solid experience handling employee relations and advising managers usually matters more.
How long does it take to become an HR business partner?

Most people need a four-year degree and then about five to eight years in HR. A common path is HR coordinator, then HR generalist, then HR business partner. People with strong generalist experience, a certification, or a master’s degree in HR sometimes move up faster.

steps: Education

Many HR coordinators hold a bachelor’s degree in human resources, business or psychology, though some employers accept an associate degree or relevant office experience. There is no license for HR work. Courses in employment law and HR basics give a useful start.
Ways in

HR coordinator is often the first HR job itself. People also move in from administrative assistant, receptionist, office coordinator, payroll clerk or customer service roles, or from an HR internship. Care with confidential records and attention to detail matter most.
Core tasks

Learn how onboarding works end to end: offer letters, background checks, Form I-9 employment verification, often with E-Verify, benefits enrollment and setting up records in the HR information system. Coordinators also schedule interviews and keep employee files complete and private.
Certification

Certification is optional. HRCI’s Associate Professional in Human Resources (aPHR) is designed for people new to HR and requires no experience. Some coordinators later take the SHRM-CP from SHRM or the Professional in Human Resources (PHR) from HRCI as they gain experience.
Time it takes

Many people land an HR coordinator role right after school or after a year or two in office work. After a few years, coordinators often move up to HR generalist, recruiter, payroll specialist or benefits specialist roles.
qa: Can you become an HR coordinator without experience?

Yes. HR coordinator and HR assistant are among the most common entry-level HR jobs. Employers often hire recent graduates or people with administrative, office or customer service experience. An HR internship, a degree in HR or business, and the aPHR certification can help you stand out.
What certification is good for an HR coordinator?

The Associate Professional in Human Resources (aPHR) from HRCI is built for people starting in HR and requires no HR experience, only a passing exam score. After gaining experience, many coordinators move on to the SHRM-CP from SHRM or the Professional in Human Resources (PHR) from HRCI. None of these is legally required.

steps: Education

Most HR managers and directors hold a bachelor’s degree in human resources, business administration, psychology or a related field. Useful courses cover employment law, compensation, organizational behavior and accounting. No specific degree is legally required, but employers almost always expect a four-year degree.
First job

People usually start as an HR assistant, HR coordinator, recruiter, or payroll or benefits specialist. These roles teach the daily work of hiring, onboarding, record keeping and answering employee questions, and they build the experience employers look for later.
Generalist experience

The next step is often an HR generalist or HR business partner role. Here you handle employee relations, investigations, benefits, policies and compliance with laws such as Title VII, the FLSA and FMLA. Broad experience across HR areas matters more for leadership than deep work in one area.
Professional certification

There is no state license for HR work. Many employers prefer certification, such as the SHRM-CP or SHRM-SCP from SHRM, or the PHR or SPHR from HRCI. Each requires passing an exam, and the senior credentials expect several years of HR experience.
Management and graduate study

Moving into management usually means leading a small HR team or a function like recruiting or compensation. Some people earn a master’s degree in human resources or an MBA, which many companies prefer for director roles, especially at larger organizations.
Time it takes

Reaching HR manager usually takes about five or more years of HR experience after a bachelor’s degree. Becoming an HR director often takes ten or more years, depending on company size and how quickly you take on leadership duties.
qa: Do you need a certification to be an HR manager?

No law requires a license or certification to work as an HR manager in the US. Still, many employers prefer or list credentials such as the SHRM-CP, SHRM-SCP, PHR or SPHR. These show knowledge of employment law and HR practice, and they can help when competing for manager and director roles.
How long does it take to become an HR director?

It usually takes ten or more years. Most people spend four years earning a bachelor’s degree, then several years in roles like HR coordinator, recruiter and HR generalist, followed by time as an HR manager. A master’s degree or senior certification can help, but leadership experience matters most.

steps: Education

Most HR generalists hold a bachelor’s degree in human resources, business, psychology or communications. Courses in employment law, compensation, benefits and organizational behavior help most. There is no license for HR work in the US.
First job

The usual first job is HR assistant, HR coordinator or recruiting coordinator, handling onboarding paperwork, employee files and the HR system. Some people move in from payroll, office management or recruiting. Generalist roles typically ask for a few years in such a role.
Laws to learn

Generalists apply federal and state employment law daily. Learn the FMLA, ADA, Title VII, FLSA wage and hour rules, COBRA and Form I-9 employment verification, plus your state’s leave, pay and posting rules, which often go further than federal law.
Certification

Certification is optional but common in postings. SHRM offers the SHRM-CP and SHRM-SCP. HRCI offers the Associate Professional in Human Resources (aPHR), with no experience required, and the Professional in Human Resources (PHR), which requires HR experience. Each requires passing an exam.
Time it takes

Most people reach an HR generalist title a few years after starting as an HR assistant or coordinator. Senior generalist and HR business partner roles usually ask for several more years and often a SHRM-SCP or SPHR.
qa: What certification should an HR generalist get?

The most common are the SHRM-CP from SHRM and the Professional in Human Resources (PHR) from HRCI. Both are optional, require passing an exam and are often listed as preferred in job postings. The PHR requires HR work experience. Beginners with no experience can start with HRCI’s Associate Professional in Human Resources (aPHR).
Can you become an HR generalist without experience?

Rarely in one step. Most HR generalists first work a year or more as an HR assistant, HR coordinator or recruiting coordinator. Small companies sometimes hire new graduates with HR internships as junior generalists. An HR degree, an internship and the aPHR certification can help a beginner get that first HR job.

steps: Education

Most employers ask for a bachelor’s degree in human resources, business, information systems or a related field. Courses in statistics, databases and employment law help. Some people get in with an associate degree plus strong HR or payroll experience.
Data and reporting skills

Learn advanced spreadsheet work, basic SQL and a data visualization tool. Practice building headcount, turnover and pay reports from sample data. Knowing how to keep confidential employee records secure matters as much as the technical skills.
First job

Most people start as an HR coordinator, HR assistant, payroll specialist or junior data analyst. In these roles you enter and fix data in the HR system and pull standard reports. This is how most HRIS specialists learn the software.
Certifications

No license is required in any state. Some employers value the SHRM-CP from SHRM or the PHR from HRCI as proof of HR knowledge. Training from the HR software vendor is often expected, and it is usually arranged through an employer that uses that system.
Time it takes

Expect about two to four years after a bachelor’s degree, including one to three years in an HR, payroll or data role, before moving into an HRIS or people analytics title. Senior people analytics roles often ask for deeper statistics skills or a master’s degree.
qa: Do you need a certification to become an HRIS specialist?

No. There is no license for HRIS work in any state. Employers mainly look for hands-on experience with HR software and reporting. Certifications such as the SHRM-CP or PHR can show HR knowledge, and vendor training on a specific HR system is a plus. They are rarely strict requirements.
How long does it take to become an HRIS analyst?

Most people need about two to four years after finishing a bachelor’s degree. That usually includes one to three years in HR, payroll or data analysis, where they learn the HR system and start building reports. People already working in HR can sometimes move in sooner by taking on system and reporting tasks.

steps: Education

Most employers ask for a bachelor’s degree in human resources, business administration, psychology or a related field. Courses in employment law, compensation, organizational behavior and business writing help. Some people with an associate degree or a strong office background get in through an assistant role instead.
First job

Many people start as an HR assistant, HR coordinator, recruiting coordinator or payroll clerk. These roles teach onboarding, employee records, benefits paperwork and HR software. They are the usual step before a specialist title.
Employment law basics

Learn the federal rules HR handles every day, such as the Fair Labor Standards Act, the Family and Medical Leave Act and Title VII of the Civil Rights Act. State laws on pay, leave and hiring add more, and they vary by state.
Certification

No license is required to work in HR, but many employers value certification from HRCI or SHRM. The aPHR and the SHRM-CP can be taken without prior HR work. The PHR requires HR experience. Each one needs ongoing credits to stay current.
Time it takes

Usually four years for a bachelor’s degree, then one to three years in an assistant or coordinator role before moving into a specialist job. Career changers with related office, payroll or management experience can sometimes move faster.
qa: Do you need a certification to be an HR specialist?

No. There is no state license for HR work, and certification is optional. Many employers still prefer one, such as the SHRM-CP from SHRM or the PHR from HRCI. The aPHR and the SHRM-CP suit newcomers because they do not require prior HR work experience.
How long does it take to become an HR specialist?

Most people take about five to seven years in total: four years for a bachelor’s degree, then one to three years as an HR assistant or coordinator. Someone who already has a degree in another field and moves into an HR support role can often reach a specialist job within a few years.

steps: High school basics

Most training programs and apprenticeships expect a high school diploma or GED. Math, basic physics, electrical shop and mechanical classes help, since the work involves reading wiring diagrams, measuring pressures and temperatures, and doing load calculations.
Trade school or apprenticeship

Many people take an HVAC or HVACR certificate or associate program at a technical school or community college, usually six months to two years. Others enter a registered apprenticeship, typically three to five years of paid on-the-job hours plus classroom instruction, often run by unions or contractor associations.
EPA Section 608 certification

Federal law requires EPA Section 608 certification to service or dispose of equipment containing refrigerants. There are Type I, Type II, Type III and Universal levels. Commercial and data center work involves larger systems, so most technicians earn Universal. The certification does not expire.
State or local license

Requirements vary by state and sometimes by city. Some states license HVAC technicians or mechanics, usually after documented work experience and an exam. Others license only HVAC contractors who run the business. Check your state licensing board before you start counting hours.
First job

The usual entry point is HVAC helper, apprentice or installer working under an experienced technician. Many start on residential installs or service calls, then move to commercial rooftop units, chillers, building controls and data center cooling as they gain skills.
Time it takes

Expect about six months to two years of schooling, or start an apprenticeship right away. Working fully on your own usually takes three to five years. Optional NATE certification can show employers your skill level as you advance.
qa: Do you need a license to be an HVAC technician?

Every technician who handles refrigerants needs EPA Section 608 certification under federal law. Beyond that, requirements vary by state. Some states and cities require an HVAC technician or mechanical license, often based on experience hours and an exam. Others license only contractors who run HVAC businesses, so technicians there work under the contractor’s license.
How long does it take to become an HVAC technician?

You can start as a helper or apprentice with little experience. A school certificate program takes about six months to two years, and a registered apprenticeship usually lasts three to five years. Most technicians need three to five years of combined training and field work before they handle complex commercial systems on their own.

steps: Education

Many employers ask for a bachelor’s degree in computer science, information technology or cybersecurity. Others accept an associate degree or equivalent work experience instead. The most useful coursework covers networking, operating systems, directory services and scripting, since IAM work touches all of them.
First job in IT

Most people start on an IT help desk, in desktop support or as a junior system administrator. These roles handle password resets, new account setup and Active Directory groups, which teaches how accounts and permissions really work inside a company.
Hands-on identity skills

Next comes learning the standards behind single sign-on and access control: SAML, OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, SCIM, LDAP and multi-factor authentication. Scripting in PowerShell or Python helps automate account work. Many people build a home lab using free tiers of identity platforms to practice.
Certifications

No license is required. CompTIA Security+ is a common first certification. Vendor credentials such as Microsoft’s SC-300 Identity and Access Administrator Associate, or certifications from Okta, SailPoint or CyberArk, show platform skill. CISSP comes later, since it requires several years of paid security experience.
Time it takes

Moving from a first IT job to an IAM engineer title usually takes two to five years. Many people pass through an IAM analyst or IAM administrator role first, handling access requests and reviews before designing and building identity systems.
qa: Do you need a certification to be an IAM engineer?

No license or certification is legally required. Still, many job postings list one. CompTIA Security+ is a common starting point, and vendor certifications for Microsoft Entra, Okta, SailPoint or CyberArk prove you can run the tools a company uses. Some government and defense contractor roles also require Security+ or a security clearance.
How long does it take to become an IAM engineer?

Most people need two to five years after starting in IT. A typical path is a help desk or system administrator job, then an IAM analyst or administrator role, then engineer. Someone with a related degree and strong scripting skills may move faster, while career changers often spend extra time building basic IT experience first.

steps: Education

Most employers ask for a bachelor’s degree in business, information systems, computer science, accounting or a related field. Some hire without a degree if you know the industry the software serves well, such as payroll, healthcare billing or supply chain.
Core technical skills

Learn the basics of moving data: spreadsheets, SQL, CSV imports, data mapping and cleanup. Understand APIs and system integrations at a working level. Practice writing clear requirements and running a training session for non-technical users.
First job

Common entry points are customer support, technical support, business analyst or junior implementation specialist at a software company. Others come from the customer side after helping roll out a new system at their own employer.
Product certifications

There is no license or required exam for this work. Many employers value certification in the product you implement, such as Salesforce Certified Administrator, offered through the vendor’s own program. Some senior consultants later add the PMP from PMI.
Time it takes

Usually one to three years in a support, analyst or specialist role before you lead implementations on your own. Reaching a senior consultant role often takes several more years of completed customer projects.
qa: Do you need a certification to be an implementation consultant?

No license or certification is required by law. Many employers prefer or require certification in their own product, and some pay for it after you’re hired. Vendor certifications, such as those for Salesforce, show you know the system. Project management credentials like the PMP can help later in your career.
How long does it take to become an implementation consultant?

Many people reach the title within one to three years after college by starting in customer support, technical support or an analyst role at a software company. People with deep experience in an industry, such as accounting or HR, can sometimes move in faster because they already understand the work the software supports.

steps: Education

Most people start with a bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance or economics. Accounting suits sales tax and VAT work. Transfer pricing teams often hire economics or finance graduates because the work involves financial analysis. Some people add a master’s in taxation, accounting or economics.
First job

The usual entry point is a staff or associate role in the tax group of an accounting firm or a company’s tax department. Typical titles are sales and use tax analyst, indirect tax associate, or transfer pricing analyst preparing benchmarking studies and documentation.
CPA license

No license is required to do this work. Many employers still value or expect the CPA license, especially on the accounting side. It requires passing the CPA exam, meeting education rules and completing supervised experience. Requirements vary by state.
Specialist credentials

Sales and use tax professionals can earn the CMI designation from the Institute for Professionals in Taxation. Some earn Enrolled Agent status by passing the IRS Special Enrollment Examination. Transfer pricing has no standard US credential, so people learn Section 482 regulations and the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines on the job.
Time it takes

After a four-year degree, it usually takes about three to five years of tax work to be seen as a specialist. Earning the CPA license often happens during the first few years of work, alongside growing experience with filings, audits and intercompany pricing.
qa: Do you need to be a CPA to work in indirect tax?

No. There is no license required to work in sales tax, VAT or transfer pricing. Many employers prefer CPAs, especially in accounting firms and for senior roles. Others value the CMI designation from the Institute for Professionals in Taxation or an economics background. CPA requirements, including education and supervised experience, vary by state.
How long does it take to become a transfer pricing specialist?

Most people need a bachelor’s degree in economics, finance or accounting, which usually takes four years. They then spend about three to five years as an analyst or associate doing benchmarking, intercompany pricing and documentation work. Some speed their path or move into senior roles with a master’s degree or the CPA license.

steps: Education

Most industrial designers earn a bachelor’s degree in industrial design, usually a four-year program with studio courses in sketching, model making, materials, manufacturing processes and 3D CAD. Many programs are accredited by the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD).
Portfolio

Employers hire mainly on the portfolio. It should show a few projects from research and sketches through models, CAD and final renderings, and explain the problem each design solves. Most students build it through studio work and sponsored class projects.
Internship

Most students complete one or more internships or co-ops at design consultancies or product companies before graduating. An internship is often the most direct path to a first job offer, and it adds real products to the portfolio.
No license

There is no license or required certification for industrial designers in the US. The Industrial Designers Society of America (IDSA) is the main professional group, offering events, awards and networking, but membership is optional.
First job

The usual first job is junior industrial designer or design associate, producing sketches, CAD models, prototypes and renderings under a senior designer. Some start as CAD designers or model makers. Reaching senior designer often takes several years.
Time it takes

Expect about four years for a bachelor’s degree, sometimes five with co-op terms. Career changers with a degree in another field, such as mechanical engineering or architecture, may take a master’s in industrial design, often two to three years, to build a portfolio.
qa: Do you need a license to be an industrial designer?

No. Industrial design has no state license or required certification in the US. Employers judge candidates on a portfolio of product work and their skills in sketching, prototyping and 3D CAD. Membership in the Industrial Designers Society of America is optional but can help with networking and visibility.
How long does it take to become an industrial designer?

Usually about four years. Most industrial designers complete a bachelor’s degree in industrial design, often with internships or co-op work, and start as junior designers right after graduating. Career changers may take a two- to three-year master’s program. Moving up to senior designer typically takes several more years of experience.

steps: Education

No license is required, and a bachelor’s degree is common but not always needed. Degrees in criminal justice, security management, homeland security, political science or business help. Many enter from military, law enforcement or government security work, where they already handled classified material.
Security clearance

You must be a US citizen eligible for a personnel security clearance. You cannot apply on your own: the employer sponsors it, and the background investigation, which starts with the SF-86 form, can take several months or longer. Facility Security Officers must be cleared at the level of the facility clearance.
Rules and agencies

The work follows the National Industrial Security Program Operating Manual (NISPOM), now codified in 32 CFR Part 117. The Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) oversees cleared contractors. Learn reporting duties, classified storage, visit requests and insider threat programs.
FSO training

Facility Security Officers must complete required training, usually through the Center for Development of Security Excellence (CDSE), which offers free online FSO courses. Many also earn the Industrial Security Professional (ISP) certification from NCMS once they have experience.
First job

Common first jobs are security assistant, security specialist, personnel security specialist or assistant Facility Security Officer at a defense contractor. You may process clearance actions in government systems such as DISS and NISS, track training and help prepare for DCSA reviews.
Time it takes

With a clearance and military or government security experience, you can often start right away. Without one, expect months for the clearance process. Moving up to Facility Security Officer at a larger contractor usually takes a few years of experience.
qa: How do you become a Facility Security Officer?

A cleared contractor appoints its Facility Security Officer, who must be an employee, a US citizen and cleared at the level of the facility clearance. The FSO must complete required training, usually free online courses from the Center for Development of Security Excellence (CDSE), and follow 32 CFR Part 117, the NISPOM. Many first work as security assistants or specialists.
Do you need a security clearance to work in industrial security?

Usually yes. Most industrial security roles at defense contractors require a personnel security clearance, and Facility Security Officers must be cleared at the level of the facility clearance. You cannot apply for a clearance on your own: an employer sponsors it. That is why many people enter after military or government service, already holding one.

steps: Education

Most people hold a bachelor’s degree in marketing, business, communications or a related field. A degree in the target industry also works well, such as finance for banking or computer science for developer audiences. Some employers prefer an MBA for senior roles, but it is rarely required.
Industry knowledge

This work depends on speaking the audience’s language. Many people build that knowledge by working in the industry first, for example as an engineer, banker, nurse or sales rep, before moving into marketing. Others learn it on the job by sitting in on customer calls and reading trade publications.
No license required

There is no license, registration or required exam for this work in any state. Optional marketing or product marketing certificates exist and can help show skills, but employers mostly judge candidates on past campaigns, writing samples and results they can explain.
First job

Common entry points are marketing coordinator, content marketer, product marketing associate or field marketing specialist. People coming from the industry often enter through sales engineering, customer success or developer relations, then move into a marketing role focused on that same audience.
Time it takes

Expect about four years for a degree, then usually three to seven years of marketing or industry experience before landing a manager title. People with deep industry backgrounds can sometimes move faster because that expertise is the hardest part to hire for.
qa: Do you need a certification to be an industry marketing manager?

No. There is no required license or certification for industry or solutions marketing in the US. Some people take optional product marketing or digital marketing certificates to strengthen a resume, but employers care far more about real experience, knowledge of the target industry and examples of campaigns, messaging or content you created.
How long does it take to become an industry marketing manager?

It usually takes several years. Most people finish a bachelor’s degree, then spend roughly three to seven years in marketing, sales or the target industry itself before reaching a manager role. Those who already know an industry well, such as former engineers or bankers, can sometimes move in sooner.

steps: Education

Most people hold a bachelor’s degree in computer science, engineering, information systems, or business. Some come from a field tied to the industry they cover, such as finance, health care, or manufacturing. An MBA or master’s degree helps some candidates but is rarely required.
Years inside the industry

The role depends on talking to customers as a peer, so employers want real experience on the customer’s side. Typical backgrounds include architect, engineering leader, IT director, or practitioner in banking, health care, retail, or government. Many specialists bring ten or more years of this work.
Customer-facing technical role

Many people build sales skills as a sales engineer, solutions architect, technical consultant, or professional services lead. This teaches discovery calls, demos, proposals, and working with account executives on a deal, which the specialist role assumes you already know.
Optional certifications

There is no license or required exam for this work. Some employers value vendor cloud certifications or security credentials such as CISSP. Knowing the industry’s rules, such as HIPAA in health care, often matters more than any certificate.
Time it takes

There is no standard path. Most people reach industry specialist or field CTO titles after about ten to fifteen years of combined industry and technical work. Senior field CTO roles often go to former CTOs, chief architects, or well-known experts.
First job

The usual entry is an industry solutions architect or industry specialist role at a software or cloud vendor. Some move up from sales engineering at the same company. Others are hired directly from a customer organization because of their industry reputation.
qa: Do you need a certification to become a field CTO?
