Most people earn a bachelor’s degree in computer science, computer engineering or a related field. Some add a master’s with a focus on machine learning or distributed systems. Coursework in operating systems, networking, data structures and statistics helps most.
Core technical skills

Learn Python and Linux well, then containers, Kubernetes, infrastructure as code and CI/CD pipelines. Add how GPUs are scheduled, how models are trained at scale with frameworks like PyTorch, and how trained models are served, versioned and monitored.
Optional certifications

No license or required exam exists for this work. Some people earn the Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) or a cloud provider’s machine learning or architect certification to show skills. Employers usually weigh hands-on experience more than certificates.
Portfolio projects

Build public projects that prove you can run models in production. Examples include a training pipeline on rented GPUs, a model serving setup on Kubernetes with autoscaling, or a feature store with monitoring and automated retraining.
First job

Few people start in this role directly. Common entry points are software engineer, DevOps engineer, site reliability engineer, data engineer or machine learning engineer, then moving toward the platform side that supports model training and serving.
Time it takes

Expect a four-year degree plus usually two to five years of work in software, infrastructure or data roles before holding the title. People already working in DevOps or backend engineering can often move over faster.
qa: Do you need a license to be an ML infrastructure engineer?

No. There is no state license, registration or required exam for ML infrastructure or MLOps work in the US. Employers judge candidates on experience with cloud systems, Kubernetes, GPUs and production pipelines. Optional certifications such as the Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) can help a résumé but are not required.
How long does it take to become an MLOps engineer?

Most people need about six to nine years in total. That usually means a four-year degree in computer science or a related field, followed by two to five years as a software, DevOps, site reliability or data engineer. Experienced infrastructure engineers who learn machine learning tooling can often switch in a year or two.

steps: Education

Most mobile engineers hold a bachelor’s degree in computer science, software engineering or a related field. A degree is common but not required. Many people get in through self-study, online courses or a bootcamp, as long as they can show strong programming skills.
Learn a platform

Pick iOS, Android or both. For iPhone apps, learn Swift, SwiftUI and Xcode. For Android, learn Kotlin, Jetpack Compose and Android Studio. Cross-platform tools like React Native or Flutter are also widely used. Learn Git, APIs and basic testing too.
No license needed

There is no state license, registration or required exam to work as a mobile engineer in the US. Employers judge you on your code, your published apps and your technical interviews rather than on certificates.
Build a portfolio

Publish one or more apps to the Apple App Store or Google Play. This requires a developer account with Apple or Google. Keep your code on GitHub so employers can review it. Real, working apps matter more than course certificates.
Time it takes
A computer science degree usually takes four years. Career changers who study on their own or in a bootcamp often need one to two years of steady practice before they are ready for a first job.
First job

The usual first role is junior iOS developer, junior Android developer or mobile engineering intern. Some people move over from web or backend development inside the same company, then shift to mobile work once they have built a few apps.
qa: Do you need a degree to become a mobile engineer?

No. Many employers prefer a degree in computer science or a related field, but it is not required. People without one get hired by showing published apps, clean code on GitHub and strong performance in technical interviews. Some larger companies screen more heavily for degrees, so a portfolio matters even more if you skip college.
How long does it take to become a mobile app developer?

It usually takes four years through a computer science degree. Self-taught learners and career changers often reach a junior level in one to two years of focused study and practice. Most need to build and publish a few real apps for iPhone or Android before landing a first job as a junior developer or intern.

steps: Education

A college degree is not required for the license, though many loan officers have a degree in finance, business or economics. Lenders look for sales, customer service and basic math skills, since the job means reading credit reports, income documents and loan terms.
Pre-licensing education

Loan officers at nonbank mortgage lenders and brokers must be state-licensed under the SAFE Act. The first step is at least 20 hours of NMLS-approved pre-licensing education, covering federal law, ethics and nontraditional mortgage products. Some states add their own required hours.
SAFE MLO Test

Next you pass the SAFE Mortgage Loan Originator Test with Uniform State Content through the Nationwide Multistate Licensing System and Registry (NMLS). You also submit fingerprints for an FBI background check and a credit report, and apply for a license in each state where you will lend.
Bank route

Loan officers employed by federally regulated banks and credit unions do not need a state license. They register through NMLS instead, with fingerprints and a background check but no required test or course, and receive an NMLS ID like licensed loan officers.
First job

Many people start as a loan processor, loan officer assistant or call center loan officer, or move in from real estate, banking or sales. New loan officers learn loan programs such as conventional, FHA and VA loans and how to take an application to closing.
Time it takes

Getting licensed usually takes a few weeks to two months: the course, the test, the background check and state approval. Licensed loan officers must complete at least 8 hours of NMLS-approved continuing education each year to renew.
qa: Do you need a license to be a mortgage loan officer?

It depends on your employer. Under the SAFE Act, loan officers at nonbank lenders and mortgage brokers need a state license, which requires 20 hours of pre-licensing education, the SAFE MLO Test and a background check. Loan officers at federally regulated banks and credit unions register through NMLS instead and do not need the test.
How long does it take to become a mortgage loan officer?

Usually a few weeks to two months. The 20-hour pre-licensing course can be finished in a few days, then you schedule and pass the SAFE MLO Test, clear the background and credit checks, and wait for state approval. Building a steady flow of borrowers through referrals usually takes much longer.

steps: Education

Many motion designers and animators earn a bachelor’s degree in animation, motion design, graphic design or fine arts. A degree is common but not required. Others learn through community college courses, online classes or self-study, as long as their work is strong.
Software and core skills

Learn the main tools, usually Adobe After Effects for motion graphics and Cinema 4D, Blender or Maya for 3D. Study the principles of animation, timing, typography and layout. Drawing, storyboarding and basic video editing skills also help.
No license required

There is no license, registration or required exam for this work in any state. Optional vendor certifications, such as Adobe Certified Professional, can show software skills, but employers mostly judge you by your reel and portfolio.
Demo reel and portfolio

Build a short demo reel, often one to two minutes, with your best motion work. Add a portfolio site with project breakdowns. Student projects, personal pieces, freelance jobs and internships all give you material to show.
Time it takes

Most people need about two to four years of study and steady practice before they are hired, whether through a degree or self-teaching. Moving up to senior roles usually takes several more years of studio, agency or in-house work.
First job

Common first jobs are motion design intern, junior motion designer, junior animator or production assistant at a studio, agency or in-house video team. Some people start as graphic designers or video editors and add motion work over time.
qa: Do you need a degree to be a motion designer?

No. Many motion designers have a bachelor’s degree in animation, graphic design or a related art field, and some employers prefer one. But there is no license or required credential. A strong demo reel and portfolio matter most, so self-taught designers with good work can get hired too.
How long does it take to become a motion designer?

It usually takes two to four years of study and practice to be ready for a junior role, through a degree program or self-teaching. You need time to learn tools like After Effects and build a solid demo reel. Reaching a senior level often takes several more years on the job.

steps: Education

Most network engineers hold an associate or bachelor’s degree in network administration, information technology, computer science or a related field. School usually takes two to four years. Some people enter without a degree through military training or self-study, but many employers list a degree in their postings.
Entry certification

No state license is required to work as a network engineer. Employers often expect certifications instead. Common first ones are CompTIA Network+ and Cisco’s CCNA, each earned by passing an exam. Some federal and defense jobs also ask for CompTIA Security+.
First job

The usual way in is a support role such as help desk technician, network technician, network operations center (NOC) technician or junior network administrator. People typically spend one to three years in these jobs, learning switches, routers, cabling, troubleshooting and change procedures before moving up.
Advanced certification

Moving into engineer and senior roles often goes with a professional-level certification such as Cisco’s CCNP or a Juniper certification. Cloud networking skills and certifications from major cloud providers are increasingly asked for. These exams are optional but widely recognized by employers.
Time it takes

Most people need about three to seven years in total: two to four years of school, then one to three years in a support or technician role. Someone with strong certifications and hands-on experience may move faster, without a full degree.
qa: Do you need a license to be a network engineer?

No. Network engineers do not need a state license in the US. Employers rely on certifications instead, such as CompTIA Network+, Cisco’s CCNA and later CCNP. Some federal and defense positions require specific certifications, such as CompTIA Security+, and some require a security clearance.
How long does it take to become a network engineer?

It usually takes about three to seven years. Most people spend two to four years earning an associate or bachelor’s degree, then one to three years in help desk, NOC or network technician jobs before being hired as a network engineer. Earning certifications like the CCNA along the way can shorten the path.

steps: Education

Most people start with a bachelor’s degree in computer science, electrical engineering, linguistics with programming, or math. Useful coursework covers machine learning, probability, linear algebra, algorithms, and signal processing for speech work. Many employers prefer a master’s degree, and research-heavy roles often ask for a PhD.
Core technical skills

You need strong Python and experience with deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch. Learn how transformer language models, tokenization, embeddings, and evaluation metrics work. For speech, study audio features, speech recognition, and text-to-speech. Data cleaning, training on GPUs, and deploying models as services matter as much as theory.
Projects and portfolio

There is no license or required certification for this work. Employers judge you by what you have built. Fine-tune a model for classification or translation, build a transcription pipeline, or publish open-source code. Research papers, competition results, and clear write-ups of your experiments carry real weight in hiring.
Internships and research

Internships at companies building language or voice products are a common way in. Graduate students often gain experience through university research labs, publishing at conferences in natural language processing or speech. These roles teach you to work with large datasets, shared codebases, and production constraints.
First job

Many people enter as a software engineer, machine learning engineer, data scientist, or research intern, then specialize in language or speech. Others move in from linguistics or data annotation roles after building programming skills. Junior titles include associate NLP engineer and applied scientist.
Time it takes

Expect usually four to six years from starting a bachelor’s degree to a first NLP-focused role, including a master’s or relevant work experience. A PhD path takes longer, often eight years or more in total. Career changers with software experience can sometimes shift in one to two years.
qa: Do you need a degree to become an NLP engineer?

Most NLP and speech engineers hold at least a bachelor’s degree in computer science or a related field, and many have a master’s or PhD. There is no license or required certification. Some people get hired without an advanced degree by showing strong software skills and a portfolio of working language or speech projects.
How long does it take to become an NLP engineer?

It usually takes four to six years, covering a bachelor’s degree plus a master’s degree or a year or two of software or machine learning work. Research scientist roles often require a PhD, which adds several more years. Experienced software engineers can often move into NLP work in one to two years of focused study and projects.

steps: Education

No license or specific degree is required. Many Node.js developers studied computer science, while others came through bootcamps or self-study. Start with JavaScript fundamentals, then TypeScript, asynchronous code with promises and async/await, and how HTTP, REST APIs and databases work.
Server skills

Learn to build APIs with Node.js and a framework such as Express, Fastify or NestJS. Work with SQL and NoSQL databases, authentication, testing, logging and error handling. Docker, message queues and deploying to a cloud platform are common next steps.
Portfolio

Build two or three back-end projects, such as a REST or GraphQL API with a database, user login and automated tests, and deploy them. Publish the code in a public repository with clear documentation, since employers often review it before interviews.
Certifications

Certifications are optional and rarely decide a hire. Cloud certifications can help for roles that deploy Node.js services, but employers judge most candidates on coding tests, system design questions and real projects.
First job

The usual first job is junior back-end developer, junior full-stack developer or junior software engineer. Many Node.js roles are full-stack, pairing Node.js with React or another front-end framework, so basic front-end skills widen your options.
Time it takes

A computer science degree takes about four years. Self-taught developers often need one to two years of steady practice before landing a first junior role. Reaching mid-level usually takes two to four years on the job.
qa: How long does it take to become a Node.js developer?

Many people get a first junior Node.js job after one to two years of steady study and project work, or after a four-year computer science degree. If you already know JavaScript from front-end work, moving to Node.js can take a few months, since the language is the same and you mainly learn servers, databases and APIs.
Can you become a Node.js developer without experience?

Yes, but you need proof of skill instead. Employers hiring juniors look for deployed back-end projects, such as APIs with databases, authentication and tests, published in a public repository. Internships, open-source contributions, freelance work and full-stack roles that include Node.js are common ways to gain the first experience employers ask for.

steps: Nursing degree

Most people start with a Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN), which usually takes four years. Registered nurses with an associate degree can enter RN-to-BSN or RN-to-MSN bridge programs. A few direct-entry programs accept people with a bachelor’s degree in another field.
RN license
Pass the NCLEX-RN and get a registered nurse license from your state board of nursing. Every nurse practitioner must first hold an active RN license, and you keep it throughout your career.
Work as an RN

Many NP programs prefer or require one to two years of RN experience, often in acute care or a setting tied to your chosen specialty. This is the usual first job on the way in, and it builds the clinical judgment you will need.
Graduate NP program

Earn a Master of Science in Nursing (MSN) or Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP) from an accredited program in one population focus, such as family, adult-gerontology, pediatrics or psychiatric-mental health. Programs include supervised clinical hours, and newer national standards set a minimum of 750 direct patient care hours.
Board certification

Pass a national certification exam in your population focus, given by bodies such as the AANP Certification Board or ANCC. Pediatric and neonatal or women’s health exams come from PNCB and NCC. Certification must be renewed through continuing education and practice hours.
State APRN license

Apply to your state board of nursing for an advanced practice registered nurse (APRN) license and prescriptive authority. You also need a DEA registration to prescribe controlled substances. Some states allow full independent practice, while others require a collaborating or supervising physician.
qa: How long does it take to become a nurse practitioner?

It usually takes about six to ten years from the start of college. That covers a four-year BSN, often one to two years working as an RN, and two to four years in an MSN or DNP program. Bridge and accelerated programs can shorten the path for some people.
Can a nurse practitioner see patients by video in other states?

Generally, a nurse practitioner needs a license in the state where the patient is located at the time of the visit. Telehealth NPs often hold licenses in several states. Rules on prescribing by video, especially controlled substances, and on physician collaboration vary by state, so check each state board of nursing.

steps: Nursing education

Complete a nursing program approved by your state board of nursing. An associate degree in nursing (ADN) usually takes two to three years. A bachelor’s (BSN) takes about four. People with a bachelor’s in another field can take an accelerated BSN. Many hospitals prefer or require a BSN.
Clinical training

Every approved program includes supervised clinical rotations in hospitals and other care settings, often covering adult medical-surgical care, pediatrics, maternity and mental health. These hours are built into school, so no separate supervised period is required after graduation to get an RN license.
NCLEX-RN exam

After graduating, apply to your state board of nursing and register for the NCLEX-RN, the national licensing exam developed by the NCSBN. Most states also require a criminal background check and fingerprints before issuing a license.
State license

You need a registered nurse license from the state where you practice. Requirements vary by state. States in the Nurse Licensure Compact issue a multistate license. For video or phone care, you generally must be licensed where the patient is located. Many states require continuing education for renewal.
Employer certifications

Most employers ask for Basic Life Support (BLS) certification, and units such as emergency, intensive care or pediatrics often require ACLS or PALS. Specialty certifications in areas like critical care or oncology usually come later, after you have worked in that area.
First job

Most new nurses start in a hospital, often on a medical-surgical unit, and many join a new graduate residency program. Others begin in long-term care, rehab or home health. Remote and telehealth roles usually expect a few years of hands-on experience first.
qa: Do you need a license to be a nurse?

Yes. To work as a registered nurse in the US, you must graduate from an approved nursing program, pass the NCLEX-RN and hold a license from a state board of nursing. Requirements vary by state. A multistate license under the Nurse Licensure Compact lets you practice in other member states.
How long does it take to become a registered nurse?

Usually two to four years. An associate degree in nursing takes about two to three years, and a bachelor’s takes about four. Accelerated programs for people who already have a bachelor’s degree are shorter. After graduating, most people take the NCLEX-RN and receive their state license within a few months.

steps: Education

Most observability engineers hold a bachelor’s degree in computer science, information technology or a related field. Employers also hire people without a degree who can show strong Linux, networking and scripting skills. Courses in operating systems, networks and basic statistics help most.
Core technical skills

Learn Linux, a language such as Python or Go, cloud basics, containers and Kubernetes. Then learn open-source tools like Prometheus for metrics and OpenTelemetry for traces, plus a log pipeline. Build a small lab that collects logs and metrics from an app and alerts you when it breaks.
First job

Few people start with this title. The usual way in is a role as a systems administrator, DevOps engineer, support engineer, junior site reliability engineer or software engineer. In that job you join on-call rotations, write alerts, build dashboards and learn how real systems fail.
Optional certifications

No license is required, and certifications are optional. Some people earn the Prometheus Certified Associate (PCA), OpenTelemetry Certified Associate (OTCA) or Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA), offered by the Linux Foundation and CNCF. Employers usually value hands-on experience with production systems more than any certificate.
Time it takes

Most people move into an observability role after about two to five years in operations, site reliability or software work. Counting a four-year degree, the path often takes six to nine years. Strong self-taught candidates with a good lab portfolio sometimes get there faster.
qa: Do you need a certification to become an observability engineer?

No. There is no license or required certification for this work in the US. Some people take the Prometheus Certified Associate or Certified Kubernetes Administrator exam to show their skills, but employers mostly hire based on real experience running, monitoring and troubleshooting production systems.
How long does it take to become an observability engineer?

It usually takes two to five years of work in a related role, such as systems administrator, DevOps engineer or site reliability engineer, after finishing school. With a four-year degree, that adds up to roughly six to nine years. People who build strong home labs and handle on-call work early can move faster.

steps: Education

A high school diploma is the usual minimum. Many employers prefer an associate or bachelor’s degree in business administration, office administration or a related field, especially at larger firms. Community college courses in bookkeeping, business writing and office software also help.
First job

Most office managers start as a receptionist, front desk coordinator, office assistant or administrative assistant. These roles teach you how visitors, mail, phones, scheduling, supplies and vendors work in a real office, which is the core of the manager’s job later.
Skills to build

Learn spreadsheets, word processing, shared calendars and email tools well. Pick up basic bookkeeping, purchasing, vendor contracts and facilities coordination. Practice planning events and onboarding new staff. In medical, legal or other specialized offices, learn the industry’s records and privacy rules.
No license required

There is no state license or required exam to work as an office manager. Some people earn the voluntary Certified Administrative Professional (CAP) credential from the International Association of Administrative Professionals (IAAP) to show their skills, but most employers weigh experience more heavily.
Time it takes

Expect usually two to five years in administrative support roles before stepping up. A degree can shorten that path somewhat. Small offices sometimes promote a strong assistant sooner, while larger organizations may want more experience and supervisory background.
Moving up

Many people become office manager through promotion where they already work. Taking on supply ordering, vendor relationships, event planning or supervising other front office staff shows you can run the office and makes the move easier, internally or at a new employer.
qa: Do you need a degree to be an office manager?

No. Many office managers start with a high school diploma and work their way up from receptionist or administrative assistant roles. That said, some employers, especially larger companies, prefer an associate or bachelor’s degree in business or a related field. Solid administrative experience often matters more than the degree itself.
How long does it take to become an office manager?

It usually takes two to five years of administrative experience. Most people start in an entry level office role, learn scheduling, purchasing, vendor management and visitor handling, then take on more responsibility. Promotion can come faster in small offices or for people with a business degree and some supervisory experience.

steps: Education

Most oil and gas engineers have a bachelor’s degree in petroleum, chemical, mechanical, civil or geological engineering. Petroleum engineering covers drilling, reservoirs and production. Chemical engineers often work in refineries and gas plants, while mechanical and civil engineers work on pipelines and facilities.
Internships and first job

Most engineers start through summer internships, then join an operator, service company, pipeline company or refinery as a field engineer or rotational engineer. Early years are spent on rigs, well sites or plants, often on rotating schedules far from home.
Safety training

Field workers complete safety training before going on site, such as SafeLand USA for onshore work, H2S awareness and first aid. Offshore workers take water survival and helicopter escape training and often need a TWIC card from the TSA. Drilling roles may require IADC or IWCF well control certification.
Pipeline and plant rules

Pipeline workers who perform covered tasks must be qualified under federal operator qualification rules from PHMSA. Refinery and gas plant staff work under OSHA process safety management rules. Employers provide much of this training on the job.
PE license

Engineers can take the FE exam near graduation, then the PE exam after about four years of experience. A state PE license is not always required in industry, but it is needed to sign off on engineering work for the public and helps with promotion.
Time it takes

Expect four years for a degree. Most engineers work independently after two to three years of field and office rotations. Senior roles, such as leading drilling programs, reservoir studies or a plant unit, usually take eight or more years.
qa: Do you need a license to be an oil and gas engineer?

Not always. Many oil and gas engineers work without a state license because their employer’s work falls under industrial exemptions. A PE license is needed to sign off on engineering work offered to the public, and it helps with promotion. You earn it by passing the FE exam, gaining about four years of experience and passing the PE exam.
How long does it take to become a petroleum engineer?

Usually four years for a bachelor’s degree in petroleum engineering, often with internships. New graduates then spend two to three years in field and office rotations before working independently. Earning a PE license usually takes about four years of experience after graduation, and senior technical roles often require eight or more years.

steps: Education

Most employers ask for a bachelor’s degree in business, economics, industrial engineering, statistics, finance or a related field. Courses in statistics, process improvement and spreadsheets matter more than the exact major. Some people enter with an associate degree plus strong work experience in operations.
Data and tool skills

Build hands-on skill in Excel, including pivot tables and lookups, plus basic SQL and a dashboard tool such as Tableau or Power BI. Practice turning raw numbers into a short finding: what is slow, what is costly and what could be automated.
Optional certifications

No license or exam is required for this work. Some people add a Lean Six Sigma Green Belt, such as the ASQ Certified Six Sigma Green Belt, or a vendor certification in a data tool. These can help a resume, but employers usually weigh experience and skills more.
First job

The usual way in is an operations associate, operations coordinator, junior data analyst or internship role. Many analysts also move up from customer support, logistics, scheduling or administrative jobs where they already know the daily processes and start tracking and fixing them.
Time it takes

Expect about four years for a bachelor’s degree, then often one to two years in an associate or coordinator role before taking a full analyst title. People switching from a related operations job can sometimes move over faster by showing process improvements they led.
qa: Do you need a certification to be an operations analyst?

No. There is no license or required exam for operations analysts in the US. Employers mainly look for a relevant degree, spreadsheet and data skills, and experience with business processes. Lean Six Sigma or data tool certifications are optional and can help, especially when changing careers, but they rarely replace real work experience.
How long does it take to become an operations analyst?

Most people take about four years to earn a bachelor’s degree and then spend up to two years in an entry role such as operations associate or coordinator. Those already working in support, logistics or administration can often move into an analyst role sooner by learning Excel and SQL and showing measurable process improvements.

steps: Education

Most employers ask for a bachelor’s degree in business administration, management, supply chain management, industrial engineering or a field tied to their industry. Some people move up without a degree, especially in retail, restaurants, warehousing and logistics, where proven results on the floor can count as much as schooling.
First job

Most people start in a frontline or support role, such as shift supervisor, team lead, assistant store manager, operations coordinator or operations analyst. These jobs teach scheduling, inventory, vendor contacts, budgets and handling staff problems, which is the daily core of operations work.
No license required

There is no state license or required exam to work as an operations manager in the US. Some industries add their own rules. For example, many states and local health departments require a certified food protection manager in restaurants, and plants and warehouses often expect OSHA 10-Hour or 30-Hour training.
Optional certifications

Certifications are not required but can help with hiring and promotion. Common choices include CPIM or CSCP from ASCM (formerly APICS), the PMP from PMI, and Lean Six Sigma belts, which many different organizations offer. Pick the one that fits your industry, such as supply chain or manufacturing.
Time it takes

Expect four years for a bachelor’s degree, then usually three to seven years in supervisor or coordinator roles before managing operations. Larger companies and director-level jobs may prefer an MBA or another graduate degree, which adds one to two years, often taken while working.
qa: Do you need a degree to be an operations manager?

Most employers prefer a bachelor’s degree in business, management, supply chain or a related field, and larger companies often require one. Still, many operations managers in retail, food service, warehousing and logistics were promoted from frontline jobs based on their results. No license is needed, so experience running shifts, budgets and teams can open the door without a degree.
How long does it take to become an operations manager?

It usually takes several years. Most people finish a four-year bachelor’s degree, then spend about three to seven years as a supervisor, team lead, coordinator or analyst before managing operations. People who start without a degree may take longer to climb from frontline roles. An MBA can speed up moves into senior roles at larger companies.

steps: Education

Most optical engineers earn a bachelor’s degree in optical engineering, physics or electrical engineering. Only a small number of US universities offer optics-specific degrees. Many people study physics or engineering and add courses in optics, photonics, electromagnetics and lasers. Strong math and programming skills help.
Graduate study

Many employers prefer a master’s degree for lens design, laser and imaging roles. A master’s usually takes one to two years. Research jobs in lasers, sensors or semiconductor optics often ask for a PhD, which commonly takes five years or more.
Hands-on experience

Internships, co-ops and lab research matter a lot in this field. Students build skill with optical design and simulation software, lens alignment, interferometry and optical test equipment. Work in a university optics or laser lab is a common way to show practical ability.
License and clearance

No license is needed to work as an optical engineer, and a PE license is rarely required in optics. Defense, aerospace and satellite employers often require US citizenship and a security clearance, which the employer sponsors after hiring.
First job

Graduates usually start as associate or junior optical engineers, optical test engineers or photonics engineers. Some begin as optical technicians and move up. Early work often focuses on testing, alignment and supporting senior designers on lens and laser systems.
Time it takes

Expect about four years for a bachelor’s degree, plus one to two years for a master’s if you pursue one. Leading lens or optical system designs on your own commonly takes several more years of work experience.
qa: Do you need a license to be an optical engineer?

No. No state license is required to work as an optical engineer. Some engineers take the FE exam or earn a PE license, but it is rarely expected in optics. Membership in professional groups such as SPIE or Optica is optional but helps with training and networking. Defense and satellite jobs may require a security clearance.
How long does it take to become an optical engineer?

It usually takes four years to earn a bachelor’s degree in optical engineering, physics or electrical engineering. Many people add a one to two year master’s degree, which employers often prefer for design roles. Research jobs in lasers or sensors may require a PhD, which adds about five or more years.

steps: Education

Most organizational development specialists have a bachelor’s degree in human resources, psychology, business or communications. Many later earn a master’s degree in organizational development, industrial-organizational psychology or human resource management, which senior roles often expect.
First job

Few people start in organizational development. Common first jobs are HR generalist, training coordinator, learning and development specialist or HR business partner. Some come from consulting or from managing teams in other parts of a business.
Core skills

The work draws on change management, leadership development, performance management, survey design and data analysis. Specialists learn to run focus groups, analyze engagement surveys and design programs that leaders will actually use. Facilitating workshops well is a must.
Certification

No license is required. Common credentials include the CPTD from the Association for Talent Development, the SHRM-CP or SHRM-SCP, and coaching credentials from the International Coaching Federation. Many specialists also get certified to use personality, 360-degree feedback or change management tools.
Psychologist title

In most states, only people with a state psychology license may call themselves psychologists. That usually requires a doctorate, supervised experience and the EPPP exam. Most organizational development specialists never need one, since the job itself is not licensed.
Time it takes

Most people reach an organizational development role after three to five years in HR, training or management. A master’s degree adds one to two years of study, often part-time while working. Leading this work for a whole company usually takes many more years.
qa: How long does it take to become an organizational development specialist?

Usually three to five years after a bachelor’s degree. Most people first work in HR, training or management, then move into organizational development once they have designed programs or led change projects. Many also earn a master’s degree in organizational development or industrial-organizational psychology, which takes one to two years and helps with senior roles.
What certification helps in organizational development?

No certification is required, but several are respected. Common choices are the CPTD from the Association for Talent Development, the SHRM-CP or SHRM-SCP from the Society for Human Resource Management, and coaching credentials from the International Coaching Federation. Many specialists also certify in the assessment or change management methods their employer uses.

steps: Education

Most OT and product security engineers hold a bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science or cybersecurity. No license is required. People come from two sides: control systems engineers who learn security, or IT security professionals who learn how industrial and embedded systems work.
Industrial systems

Learn how PLCs, SCADA, distributed control systems and safety systems work, along with industrial protocols such as Modbus, DNP3 and EtherNet/IP. Hands-on time with real controllers, in a lab or plant, matters because safety and uptime come first in these environments.
Standards

Learn the standards your industry uses: ISA/IEC 62443 for industrial automation, NERC CIP for the bulk electric system, ISO/SAE 21434 for vehicles, and FDA premarket cybersecurity guidance for medical devices. Employers want people who can turn these requirements into designs and tests.
Certifications

Common certifications include GIAC Global Industrial Cyber Security Professional (GICSP), GIAC Response and Industrial Defense (GRID) and ISA/IEC 62443 cybersecurity certificates from ISA. They are not legally required but are widely respected in OT hiring.
First job

Many start as controls engineers, automation technicians, embedded software engineers or IT security analysts at a utility, manufacturer, carmaker or device maker, then move into security. Some begin as OT security analysts at consulting firms that assess plants and products.
Time it takes

Expect four years for an engineering or computer science degree, then usually two to five years in controls, embedded or security work before a dedicated OT or product security engineering role. Senior roles that set security for whole plants or product lines take longer.
qa: What certification is best for OT security?

No certification is legally required, but the most recognized are GIAC Global Industrial Cyber Security Professional (GICSP), GIAC Response and Industrial Defense (GRID) and the ISA/IEC 62443 certificates from ISA. Engineers at electric utilities also need to know NERC CIP standards. Hands-on experience with PLCs and control networks often counts as much as any certificate.
Can you move into OT security from IT security?

Yes, and many do. IT security professionals need to learn how industrial control systems, PLCs and protocols like Modbus and DNP3 work, and why safety and uptime limit patching and scanning. A home lab with a small PLC, study for the GICSP and time spent at a plant or utility help make the move.

steps: Education

Most packaging engineers have a bachelor’s degree in packaging science or packaging engineering, offered at a small number of US universities, or in mechanical, materials, chemical or industrial engineering. Semiconductor packaging engineers usually study electrical, materials or mechanical engineering, often to a master’s or PhD.
Internships and co-ops

Many students complete co-ops or internships at consumer goods, food, medical device or electronics makers. These give hands-on experience with materials, package testing and production lines, and they are the most common route to a first full-time offer.
First job

The usual first role is an entry-level packaging engineer, packaging technician or materials engineer. You design and test packages, work with suppliers and production, and run drop, vibration and compression tests using procedures from groups such as ISTA and ASTM International.
Rules and standards

Rules depend on the product. Food packaging must meet FDA food contact rules, and medical device packaging follows sterile barrier standards such as ISO 11607. Anyone who prepares hazardous materials shipments must receive DOT hazmat training. Chip packaging engineers follow industry reliability and thermal testing standards.
Certification

No license is required for most packaging work. The Institute of Packaging Professionals offers the CPP (Certified Packaging Professional) for experienced engineers. Some engineers in regulated fields also earn a PE license, but few packaging jobs require it.
Time it takes

Expect four years for a bachelor’s degree, often with internships along the way. Engineers usually lead their own package designs within two to five years. Semiconductor packaging roles often require a graduate degree, which adds two to six years.
qa: How long does it take to become a packaging engineer?

Usually about four years. Most packaging engineers earn a bachelor’s degree in packaging science or another engineering field and complete internships or co-ops, then start as entry-level engineers. Leading package design projects typically takes another two to five years. Semiconductor packaging roles often require a master’s or PhD, which adds more time.
What certification is there for packaging engineers?

The main one is the CPP (Certified Packaging Professional) from the Institute of Packaging Professionals, aimed at engineers with work experience. Many also train in transit test procedures from ISTA. Anyone who prepares hazardous materials shipments must complete DOT hazmat training. No state license is required for most packaging jobs.

steps: Education

Most paralegals hold an associate degree in paralegal studies or a bachelor’s degree plus a paralegal certificate. Many employers prefer programs approved by the American Bar Association (ABA). Courses cover legal research, writing, civil procedure, contracts and e-discovery tools. Some people enter with an unrelated bachelor’s degree and learn on the job.
Licensing rules

Most states do not license paralegals, and they work under a lawyer’s supervision. California sets education and continuing education rules for anyone using the title. A few states, such as Oregon and Arizona, now license paraprofessionals to handle limited matters on their own. Requirements vary by state.
Voluntary certification

Certification is optional but valued by many employers. Common options are NALA’s Certified Paralegal (CP) exam and NFPA’s PCCE and PACE exams. Each has its own education or experience requirements, and keeping the credential usually means continuing legal education.
Time it takes

An associate degree usually takes about two years. A certificate program for people who already hold a bachelor’s degree often takes several months to a year. Building enough experience for advanced certification or senior roles usually takes a few more years.
First job

Many start as a legal assistant, legal secretary, docketing clerk or records clerk in a law firm, corporate legal department or government office. Others move in from contract administration or compliance support. Strong skills with document management, e-filing and contract tracking tools help with the step up.
qa: Do you need a license to be a paralegal?

In most states, no. Paralegals usually work under a lawyer’s supervision without a state license. California sets education and continuing education rules for the title, and Oregon and Arizona license paraprofessionals for limited independent work. Many paralegals choose voluntary certification, such as NALA’s Certified Paralegal or NFPA’s PACE, to show their skills to employers.
How long does it take to become a paralegal?

It usually takes about two years through an associate degree in paralegal studies. People who already have a bachelor’s degree can often finish a paralegal certificate in several months to a year. Some start sooner as legal assistants and learn the work on the job, then add a certificate or certification later.

steps: Education

Most employers ask for a bachelor’s degree in business, marketing, communications or a related field. No specific major is required. Some companies hire on proven sales or account experience alone, especially at startups and smaller software firms.
No license required

There is no license, registration or required exam for this work in the US. Optional certifications in partner or channel management, sales methods, or the CRM and partner platforms a company uses can help a resume but are rarely required.
First job

Most people start in a customer-facing role such as sales development representative, account executive, account manager, customer success manager or business development representative. Some move over from channel sales support, alliances coordinator or marketing roles that already work with partners.
Build partner skills

Learn to negotiate partner agreements, plan joint marketing and co-selling, track partner-sourced revenue in a CRM, and know the product well enough to support integrations. Asking to take on a few reseller or agency accounts in your current job is a common way in.
Time it takes

It usually takes two to five years of sales, account management or business development experience before a first partner manager or channel manager title. Senior roles often expect more years and a clear record of growing revenue through partners.
qa: Do you need a degree to be a partner manager?

Most job postings ask for a bachelor’s degree, often in business, marketing or communications, but no specific major is required. There is no license or required exam. Many employers weigh experience more heavily, so a strong record in sales, account management or business development can matter as much as the degree.
How long does it take to become a partner manager?

Partner manager is rarely an entry-level job. Most people spend two to five years in sales, account management, customer success or business development first. Counting a four-year degree, the path usually takes six to nine years. Taking on partner accounts early in a sales role can shorten it.

steps: Education

Most partner marketing managers hold a bachelor’s degree in marketing, business, communications or a related field. Employers rarely ask for a specific major. Coursework in marketing strategy, analytics and writing helps. Some people come from sales or business development instead and learn marketing on the job.
Entry-level marketing role

The usual way in is a general marketing job such as marketing coordinator, marketing specialist, field marketing specialist or channel marketing coordinator. These roles teach campaign planning, event support, email programs and working with sales teams. Some people start in partner operations or alliances support and move into marketing from there.
Partner program experience

Next, people take on work with resellers, distributors or marketplace partners. This means building co-branded content, running joint campaigns, managing market development funds, and tracking partner-sourced leads in CRM and partner relationship management tools. Showing that joint campaigns produced pipeline or revenue is what moves a person toward the manager title.
Licenses and certifications

No license, registration or exam is required to do this work in the US. There is no single standard credential. Some people take digital marketing or marketing automation certificates, or complete the training programs that large technology vendors offer their partners, but employers usually weigh hands-on campaign results more.
Time it takes

Reaching a partner marketing manager title usually takes about three to five years of marketing experience after a bachelor’s degree. People with prior channel sales or alliances experience sometimes move in faster. Senior roles that own a whole partner ecosystem or several regions often expect more years.
First manager job

The first job with this title is often at a software, cloud or technology hardware company that sells through resellers or online marketplaces. It may be called channel marketing manager, alliance marketing manager or partner marketing manager, and often covers a single partner type, product line or region.
qa: Do you need a degree to become a partner marketing manager?

Most job postings ask for a bachelor’s degree, usually in marketing, business or communications. It is not a legal requirement, and no license applies to this work. People without a degree can get in through strong experience in channel sales, business development or marketing coordination, especially if they can show campaigns that produced leads or revenue with partners.
How long does it take to become a partner marketing manager?

It usually takes about three to five years of marketing experience after finishing a bachelor’s degree. Most people start as a marketing coordinator or specialist, then take on channel or partner work before earning the manager title. Those coming from partner sales or alliances roles can sometimes make the move sooner.

steps: Education

Most payments engineers hold a bachelor’s degree in computer science, software engineering or a related field. No law requires a degree, and some people enter through self-study or a coding program, but many banks and fintech employers still list a degree in their postings.
Backend engineering skills

Build strong backend skills first: a server language, SQL databases, APIs and distributed systems. Payments work leans hard on database transactions, idempotent requests, retries, reconciliation and careful handling of money amounts so no cent is lost to rounding or duplicate charges.
Payments domain knowledge

Learn how money actually moves: card authorization, capture, settlement, refunds and chargebacks; ACH transfers under Nacha rules; wires; and message formats such as ISO 8583 and ISO 20022. Double-entry bookkeeping is the basis for keeping a ledger correct.
Security and compliance

There is no license for this work. Employers expect familiarity with PCI DSS for handling card data, plus encryption and tokenization. Optional credentials exist, such as Nacha’s Accredited ACH Professional (AAP), but most engineers learn compliance on the job.
First job

The usual way in is a general backend or software engineer role, often at a bank, fintech, online store or software company. Many people move onto a billing, checkout or payments team after proving themselves, then specialize from there.
Time it takes

Expect about four years for a degree, then usually two to five years of backend engineering before being trusted with core payments systems. Engineers who join a payments team early can specialize sooner.
qa: Do you need a license or certification to be a payments engineer?

No. There is no state or federal license for payments engineers in the US. Employers care about software skills and knowledge of rules like PCI DSS and Nacha’s ACH rules. Optional credentials such as the Accredited ACH Professional (AAP) exist, but most payments engineers have none and learn the domain on the job.
How long does it take to become a payments engineer?

It usually takes six to nine years in total. That is about four years for a computer science or related degree, then two to five years working as a backend software engineer. People who land on a billing or payments team early in their careers often specialize faster.

steps: Education

Most employers ask for a high school diploma, and many prefer an associate or bachelor’s degree in accounting, business or finance. Courses in bookkeeping, payroll accounting and spreadsheets help most, since the work is built on accurate numbers and records.
Learn payroll rules

You need to understand federal and state income tax withholding, Social Security and Medicare taxes, overtime under the Fair Labor Standards Act, and year-end forms like the W-2. State payroll and wage laws differ, so you also learn the rules where your employees work.
First job

Most people start as a payroll clerk, payroll assistant, accounts payable clerk or HR assistant. In these roles you enter hours, fix pay errors, answer employee questions and learn the payroll software your employer uses under a more senior specialist.
Optional certification

No license is required. Many specialists earn the Fundamental Payroll Certification (FPC) from PayrollOrg, formerly the American Payroll Association, which is open to beginners. The more advanced Certified Payroll Professional (CPP) requires payroll work experience before you can sit for the exam.
Time it takes

With a diploma or degree, most people move from a clerk or assistant job to a payroll specialist role in about one to three years. Earning the FPC or prior experience with payroll software can shorten that time.
qa: Do you need a certification to be a payroll specialist?

No. There is no state or federal license for payroll work, and many specialists are hired on experience alone. Certifications such as the FPC or CPP from PayrollOrg are voluntary, but some employers prefer or reward them because they show you know tax withholding and wage law.
How long does it take to become a payroll specialist?

It usually takes one to three years. Many people start as a payroll clerk or assistant right after high school or an associate degree, learn the software and tax rules on the job, and then move up to a specialist role once they can run payroll on their own.

steps: Education

Most employers ask for a bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering or electronics engineering technology. Courses in circuits, electromagnetics and signal integrity matter most. Some layout designers enter with a two-year electronics or drafting degree and build their engineering skills on the job.
Build real boards

Design and order your own boards in school or at home with a free tool such as KiCad. Handle schematic capture, footprints, routing and assembly, then power the boards up and debug them. A small portfolio of working boards often counts for more than grades.
Certification, not license

No state license is required, and a PE license is rarely needed for this work. Some designers earn the IPC CID or CID+ certification, which covers board design standards such as IPC-2221. It is optional, but many employers recognize it.
First job

Common entry roles are junior PCB layout designer, CAD librarian building parts and footprints, hardware test engineer or electronics technician. Lab work with oscilloscopes, soldering and rework teaches how layout choices behave on real boards during bring-up.
Time it takes
Expect about four years for a bachelor’s degree. After that, it usually takes two to five years of work before you lead complex boards on your own, such as high-speed, high-layer-count or RF designs.
qa: Do you need a degree to become a PCB design engineer?

Most PCB design engineer jobs ask for a bachelor’s degree in electrical or computer engineering or electronics engineering technology. Some people start as layout designers or technicians with a two-year degree and move up through experience. A portfolio of boards you designed, built and debugged helps either way.
Is there a certification for PCB designers?

Yes. IPC offers the Certified Interconnect Designer (CID) and the advanced CID+ certification, which test knowledge of board design standards and manufacturing rules. Neither is legally required, and no state license applies to this work. Many employers still view the CID as a useful sign that a designer knows industry standards.

steps: Education

Many penetration testers hold a bachelor’s degree in computer science, cybersecurity or information technology, but a degree is not strictly required. Employers care most that you understand networking, Linux and Windows systems, web applications, and scripting in a language such as Python or Bash.
First IT job

Most people start in a related role such as help desk, system administrator, network administrator or security operations center (SOC) analyst. These jobs teach how real networks are built and defended, which is exactly what you will later attack.
Hands-on practice

Build a home lab, use legal practice platforms and capture-the-flag competitions, and write up what you find. A portfolio of reports, scripts or responsibly disclosed bugs shows employers you can do the work. Never test any system without written permission from its owner.
Certifications

No state license is required. Employers often ask for certifications such as CompTIA Security+, CompTIA PenTest+, CEH, GPEN or OSCP. The OSCP, a timed hands-on exam where you break into machines and write a report, is widely respected. Government roles may also require a security clearance.
Time it takes

It usually takes two to five years to go from starting in IT to a first penetration testing role. People with a security degree and strong hands-on skills sometimes move faster. Career changers without IT experience often take longer.
First job

The usual entry title is junior or associate penetration tester, often at a security consulting firm or on an internal red team. You work under senior testers, run scoped tests, and write clear reports that explain each finding and how to fix it.
qa: Do you need a license to be a penetration tester?

No. There is no state or federal license for penetration testing in the US. Employers look instead at certifications such as OSCP, CompTIA PenTest+, CEH or GPEN, plus proven hands-on skill. Every test must be done with written authorization from the system owner, because unauthorized access is a crime under federal and state law.
How long does it take to become a penetration tester?

Most people take two to five years. That usually includes a degree or self-study, one or more years in IT or security operations, and time preparing for a hands-on certification like the OSCP. Someone already working as a system administrator or SOC analyst can often make the move within one to two years of focused practice.

steps: Education

Most employers ask for a bachelor’s degree in human resources, business, psychology or a related field. Some will accept an associate degree or relevant office experience instead, especially for coordinator-level roles. Courses in employment law, payroll basics and data handling are especially useful.
First job

Most people start as an HR assistant, HR coordinator, recruiting coordinator or HR administrator. In these roles you handle paperwork such as Form I-9 verification, offer letters, new hire setup and employee records. Some people move over from office administration, payroll or customer support.
Systems and compliance skills

On the job you learn the HR information system, or HRIS, plus payroll and benefits platforms. You also learn the basics of federal rules such as the FLSA and FMLA. State rules on final pay, leave and records differ, so you learn the ones your employer operates in.
Optional certification

No license is required. Many specialists earn a certification to show their knowledge. Common ones are the aPHR or PHR from HRCI and the SHRM-CP from SHRM. Some require a set amount of HR experience before you can take the exam, depending on your education.
Time it takes

With a degree, people usually spend one to three years in an assistant or coordinator role before taking a people operations specialist title. Without a degree, the move often takes longer and depends on hands-on experience with HR processes.
qa: Do you need a certification to work in people operations?

No. There is no license or required certification for people operations work in the US. Many employers do value the SHRM-CP from SHRM or the aPHR or PHR from HRCI, and some job postings list them as preferred. Experience with onboarding, HR data and an HRIS usually matters more for getting hired.
How do you get into people operations with no experience?

Most people start in an entry-level role such as HR assistant, HR coordinator or recruiting coordinator. Office administration, payroll or customer support jobs can also lead in. Learning an HRIS, basic employment law and careful record keeping helps. An entry-level certification like the aPHR from HRCI can show employers you understand the basics.

steps: Education

Most people start with a bachelor’s degree in marketing, business, economics, communications or statistics. No degree is legally required, and some people enter from unrelated fields, but many employers list a bachelor’s degree in their postings. Coursework in statistics, consumer behavior and data analysis is especially useful.
Platform certifications

There is no license for this work. Employers often expect platform credentials instead, such as the Google Ads certifications earned through Google Skillshop, the Google Analytics certification and the Meta Certified Media Buying Professional exam offered through Meta Blueprint. These show you know the tools but do not replace real campaign results.
Hands-on practice

Build skill by running small campaigns, even with a tiny budget for a personal project, a friend’s business or a nonprofit. Learn conversion tracking, A/B testing, audience targeting, bid strategies and attribution. Strong spreadsheet skills matter, and basic SQL or a data visualization tool helps you stand out.
First job

The usual entry role is PPC specialist, paid search associate, paid social coordinator or digital marketing coordinator, often at an advertising agency. Agencies expose you to many clients, budgets and channels quickly. Some people move over from related roles such as SEO, email marketing, sales operations or data analysis.
Time it takes

Moving from an entry role to performance marketing manager usually takes three to five years. Promotion depends on showing that campaigns you ran lowered cost per customer or raised return on ad spend. Managing larger budgets and more channels, then supervising other specialists, is the typical path upward.
qa: Do you need a license to be a performance marketing manager?

No. There is no state or federal license for buying or managing online ads in the US. Instead, employers look for platform certifications such as Google Ads and Meta Certified Media Buying Professional, plus a track record of campaigns that brought in customers at a good cost. Proven results usually matter more than any credential.
How long does it take to become a performance marketing manager?

Most people spend about four years earning a bachelor’s degree, then three to five years in roles like PPC specialist or paid social coordinator before reaching manager. People who switch from related work such as SEO or data analysis can sometimes move faster if they already understand tracking, testing and budget decisions.

steps: Prepharmacy courses

Most pharmacy schools ask for two to four years of college first, with biology, general and organic chemistry, physics, calculus and English. Many students finish a bachelor’s degree before applying. Work or volunteer time in a pharmacy, often as a technician, strengthens an application.
Doctor of Pharmacy

Every state requires a Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD) from a program accredited by the Accreditation Council for Pharmacy Education (ACPE). Programs usually take four years, and some accelerated ones take three. The last year is mostly full-time rotations in community, hospital and other practice settings.
Intern hours

Pharmacy students register as pharmacy interns with their state board of pharmacy. Supervised practice hours are required for a license, and most are earned during school rotations. Many students also work part-time as interns in a retail or hospital pharmacy, which often leads to a job offer.
Licensing exams

To get a state license you pass the North American Pharmacist Licensure Examination (NAPLEX) and a pharmacy law exam, usually the Multistate Pharmacy Jurisprudence Examination (MPJE). A few states, such as California, use their own law exam. Both national exams are run by the National Association of Boards of Pharmacy.
Residency

Residency is optional but often expected for hospital and clinical jobs. A PGY1 residency lasts one year, and a specialized PGY2 adds a second. Many residencies are accredited by ASHP. Some pharmacists later earn specialty certification from the Board of Pharmacy Specialties.
First job and timeline

Most new pharmacists start as staff pharmacists in a retail chain, hospital or mail-order pharmacy. Expect six to eight years after high school to become licensed, plus one or two years for residency. Pharmacists must complete continuing education to renew their license.
qa: Do you need a license to be a pharmacist?

Yes. Every state requires pharmacists to be licensed by its board of pharmacy. You need a PharmD from an ACPE-accredited program, the required intern hours, and passing scores on the NAPLEX and a pharmacy law exam, usually the MPJE. Licenses are renewed with continuing education, and working in another state usually means getting licensed there too.
How long does it take to become a pharmacist?

Usually six to eight years after high school. Most students spend two to four years on prerequisite college courses, then four years in a PharmD program, or three in an accelerated one. Passing the NAPLEX and a law exam follows. Pharmacists aiming for hospital or clinical roles often add one or two years of residency.

steps: Education

Most employers want a high school diploma or GED. High school math, chemistry and biology help, since technicians count doses, measure and convert units. Some states and employers set a minimum age, often 18, and require a clean background check and drug screening.
Training

Many technicians learn on the job through employer training programs at retail and hospital pharmacies. Others take a certificate or associate program, which can run from a few months to two years. Programs accredited by ASHP and ACPE include practical work in a pharmacy and prepare students for certification exams.
State registration

Most states require pharmacy technicians to register with or be licensed by the state board of pharmacy before working. Many issue a trainee registration while you train. Requirements vary by state, and some states require national certification within a set time after you start.
Certification

The main national credential is the Certified Pharmacy Technician (CPhT) from the Pharmacy Technician Certification Board, earned by passing the PTCE. The National Healthcareer Association offers another route through its ExCPT exam. Certified technicians complete continuing education to keep the credential. Hospital jobs, especially sterile compounding, often ask for certification.
First job

Most people start as a pharmacy technician or technician trainee at a retail pharmacy, counting pills, entering prescriptions, handling insurance and serving customers. With experience and extra training, technicians can move into hospital, sterile compounding, mail-order or pharmacy billing roles.
Time it takes

You can often start as a trainee within weeks. Getting certified usually takes a few months to a year of training or study. Moving into specialized hospital or compounding roles usually takes one to two more years of experience and added training.
qa: Do you need a license to be a pharmacy technician?

In most states, yes. Pharmacy technicians usually must register with or be licensed by the state board of pharmacy, often after a background check. Some states also require national certification, such as the CPhT earned through the PTCE or the ExCPT exam. A few states have lighter rules, so requirements vary by state.
How long does it take to become a pharmacy technician?

Often a few months. Many people start as trainees within weeks and learn on the job, while certificate programs usually last from a few months to a year, and associate degrees take about two years. Passing the PTCE or ExCPT exam can follow as soon as training is complete.

steps: Bachelor’s degree

Start with a bachelor’s degree in a field like computer science, math, statistics, physics, chemistry, biology or engineering. Join a faculty research lab as an undergraduate if you can. Research experience and strong letters from professors matter more for PhD admission than grades alone.
PhD program admission

Apply to a doctoral program in your field. Many US science and engineering PhD programs fund students through research or teaching assistantships. Some programs still ask for the GRE, but many no longer do, so requirements vary by school.
Research and publications

Pick an advisor and build a research record. Employers hiring PhD interns look for papers at peer-reviewed conferences or journals, strong coding skills, and work that matches their team’s focus. In AI, papers at venues such as NeurIPS or ICML carry a lot of weight.
Work authorization

There is no license or exam for this work. International students on F-1 visas usually need Curricular Practical Training (CPT) approved by their school before starting a paid US internship. Rules differ by school, so check with your international student office early.
Time it takes

Most students land a first internship after their first or second year of the PhD. Internships usually run about three months in summer, though some run in fall or spring. A full PhD often takes four to six years.
First job

The usual role is a research intern, research scientist intern or applied scientist intern at a company or national lab. Strong interns often get return offers, and many later join full time as research scientists after finishing the degree.
qa: Do you need to be in a PhD program to be a PhD intern?

Yes, in almost all cases. PhD internships are meant for students currently enrolled in a doctoral program, usually in computer science, engineering or a natural science. Some postings also accept master’s students with strong research records, but most require active PhD enrollment and an expected graduation date.
When should PhD students apply for research internships?

Many companies open summer research internship postings in the fall, and hiring often continues into winter and early spring. Applying early helps. Students usually reach out through job postings, advisors, conference contacts or former interns, and interviews often include a research talk, coding questions or a discussion of past papers.

steps: Basic requirements

Most employers want you to be at least 18, with a high school diploma or GED. You will need to pass a criminal background check and fingerprinting. A clean record, a valid driver’s license for patrol roles, and good written English for incident reports help a lot.
Pre-assignment training

Many states require a short training course before you can work, covering legal powers, use of force, report writing and emergency response. Some states also require more training in your first months on the job and refresher training every year. Requirements vary by state.
State guard license

Most states require unarmed security officers to hold a state guard license or registration, such as California’s guard card. It is usually issued by a state licensing board or the state police after training and a background check. A few states have no statewide license, though some cities do.
Armed officer permit

Armed posts need a separate permit in most states. This usually means firearms training, a range qualification, extra background screening, and often a minimum age of 21. You must requalify on a regular schedule to keep the permit active.
First job

Most people start as unarmed officers at an office building, store, hospital, warehouse or event, often through a contract security company. From there, officers move into patrol, CCTV control room work, supervisor roles, or executive and travel protection, which often favors military or police experience.
Time it takes

Getting into an entry-level unarmed job usually takes a few days to a few weeks, depending on training and how fast the state processes your license. Moving up to supervisor or specialist roles usually takes several years, and certifications like the Certified Protection Officer or ASIS International’s PSP come later.
qa: Do you need a license to be a security guard?

In most states, yes. Unarmed security officers usually need a state guard license or registration, which requires a background check, fingerprints and a short training course. Armed officers need an additional firearms permit. A few states have no statewide license, but some cities and counties set their own rules, so check where you plan to work.
How long does it take to become a security officer?

Usually a few days to a few weeks. You complete any required pre-assignment training, apply for your state license, and wait for the background check to clear. Many employers hire you while your application is pending if the state allows it. Becoming an armed officer takes longer because of firearms training and a separate permit.

steps: Bachelor’s degree

Most future physicians earn a bachelor’s degree in any major while taking premedical courses: biology, general and organic chemistry, physics and often biochemistry. Clinical volunteering, shadowing physicians and research experience strengthen a medical school application.
MCAT

Nearly all US medical schools require the MCAT, a standardized exam covering biology, chemistry, physics, psychology and critical reasoning. Most applicants take it about a year before they hope to start medical school, then apply through a centralized application service.
Medical school

Medical school usually takes four years and leads to an MD or DO degree. The first years focus on classroom science, and the later years on clinical rotations. MD students take USMLE Step 1 and Step 2 CK; DO students take COMLEX-USA Levels 1 and 2.
Residency as first job

Graduates enter residency through the National Resident Matching Program, called the Match. The first job is resident physician, often called an intern in year one. Residency lasts three to seven years by specialty, such as three for family medicine and five or more for general surgery.
State license and boards

Every state requires a medical license from its state medical board. Most require passing USMLE Step 3 or COMLEX-USA Level 3 and completing at least one year of residency, though rules vary by state. Most employers also expect board certification in a specialty after residency.
Time it takes

Expect about 11 to 15 years after high school: four years of college, four of medical school and three to seven of residency. An optional fellowship to subspecialize, for example in cardiology, usually adds one to three more years.
qa: How long does it take to become a physician?

It usually takes 11 to 15 years after high school. That includes a four-year bachelor’s degree, four years of medical school and a residency of three to seven years depending on the specialty. Physicians who complete a fellowship to subspecialize, such as in cardiology or oncology, typically spend one to three more years in training.
Do you need a license to be a physician?

Yes. Every state requires physicians to hold a medical license from its state medical board before practicing independently. Licensing usually requires a medical degree, passing all steps of the USMLE or COMLEX-USA, and some completed residency training. Requirements vary by state, and doctors seeing patients online generally need a license in the state where the patient is located.

steps: Bachelor’s and prerequisites

Before PA school, you need a bachelor’s degree, often in biology, health science or chemistry, with prerequisites such as anatomy, physiology, microbiology, chemistry and statistics. Most programs take applications through CASPA, the Central Application Service for Physician Assistants.
Patient care experience

Most PA programs expect hands-on patient care hours before you apply. Common jobs for this are emergency medical technician, medical assistant, certified nursing assistant, medical scribe, phlebotomist or paramedic. Required hours vary widely by program.
PA program

PA programs are graduate programs, usually master’s degrees, accredited by the ARC-PA. They usually last about two to three years and combine classroom study with clinical rotations in family medicine, internal medicine, surgery, pediatrics, emergency medicine and other fields.
National exam

Graduates must pass the PANCE, the Physician Assistant National Certifying Exam from the NCCPA, to earn the PA-C credential. Keeping it requires continuing medical education every two years and passing a recertification exam about every ten years.
State license

All states require PAs to hold a state license, usually issued by the state medical board, and passing the PANCE is required to get one. PAs practice under supervision or collaboration agreements with physicians, and the rules vary by state. Prescribing controlled substances also requires DEA registration.
Time it takes

Expect four years for a bachelor’s degree, often a year or more of patient care experience, and about two to three years of PA school. In total, most PAs start practicing six to eight years after high school. Optional postgraduate residencies add about a year.
qa: How long does it take to become a physician assistant?

Usually six to eight years after high school. That includes a four-year bachelor’s degree with science prerequisites, often a year or more of hands-on patient care work, and a PA program that lasts about two to three years. After graduating, you must pass the PANCE and get a state license before you can practice.
Do you need a license to be a physician assistant?
